rdfs:comment: An object attached to or associated with the subject — typically images, files, or media.
notes: ActivityStreams' attachment slot — used by ActivityPub posts to carry media (images, video, polls). Repeat for multiple attachments. Each value is typically a typed object like `urn:solid:Image` or `as:Document` with a `url` and `mediaType`.

rdfs:label: attributedTo
rdfs:comment: An entity to which the object is attributed — typically the author or creator.
notes: ActivityStreams' general-purpose author/origin pointer — works for Notes, Articles, Activities, Images. The value is typically an Actor (Person, Application, Group, Service). For dcterms-style bibliographic authorship use `urn:solid:creator`; for PROV-grade attribution use `prov:wasAttributedTo`.

rdfs:label: audience
rdfs:comment: The intended audience of the object — who it is targeted at, regardless of who actually receives it.
notes: Used to declare semantic targeting (e.g. "this is for friends", "this is for the engineering team") independently of `as:to`/`as:cc` (which are wire-level addressing). The value can be an Actor, Collection, or symbolic IRI like `as:Public`.

rdfs:label: author
rdfs:comment: The author of the creative work.
notes: Schema.org's narrow authorship predicate, meant for the author of a CreativeWork. For general authorship/creation attribution use `urn:solid:creator` (dcterms); for ActivityStreams social content use `urn:solid:attributedTo`. Repeat for co-authors.

rdfs:label: available
rdfs:comment: The date or period when the resource became (or will become) available.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:issued` (formal publication): `available` is when the resource starts to be obtainable, which can differ from publication for embargoed papers, scheduled releases, or pre-orders. Can be a single date or an ISO 8601 interval.

rdfs:label: basedNear
rdfs:comment: A geographic location near where the subject is based.
notes: Intentionally fuzzy — "near", not "at" — so people can share a city or region without revealing a precise address. Value is typically a geo:SpatialThing or `schema:Place`. For a precise postal address, prefer `vcard:hasAddress` or `schema:address`.

rdfs:label: bcc
rdfs:comment: Blind carbon-copy recipients of the object — recipients hidden from other receivers.
notes: Email-style bcc: recipients receive the activity but their addresses MUST be stripped from the object before it's seen by other receivers. Use sparingly — `bcc` semantics are easily mishandled by misbehaving servers, leaking what was meant to be private.

examples.title: Note privately delivered alongside public one

rdfs:label: bday
rdfs:comment: The full date of birth of the subject (year-month-day).
notes: vCard's full birth date — `xsd:date` with year ("1990-03-14"), distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:birthday` which is just `mm-dd` (no year). Use `bday` when you need the actual year for age calculation; use `birthday` for anniversary semantics without revealing age.

examples.title: vCard with a full birth date

rdfs:label: bibliographicCitation
rdfs:comment: A bibliographic reference for the resource — a formatted citation string.
notes: A formatted citation string as you'd see in a reference list ("Author, A. (2026). Title. Journal, vol(issue), pages."). For machine-actionable citations with structured metadata, prefer linking to a `dcterms:BibliographicResource` via `urn:solid:references` instead.

jsonld.urn:solid:bibliographicCitation: Liddell, A. (2026). On Wonderlands. Solid Journal, 1(1), 1-10.

rdfs:label: birthday
rdfs:comment: The birthday of the agent — month and day, formatted as mm-dd.
notes: FOAF format is bare `mm-dd` (no year), preserving the recurring-anniversary semantics. For a full date of birth (with year), prefer `vcard:bday` or `schema:birthDate` which take an `xsd:date`.

rdfs:label: broadMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that a Concept in another scheme is broader than this Concept.
notes: Cross-scheme version of `urn:solid:broader`. Use across SKOS schemes when you want to say "the closest broader concept in *that* vocabulary is this one". Inverse of `urn:solid:narrowMatch`.

rdfs:label: broader
rdfs:comment: A broader (parent) SKOS Concept in a hierarchy — "category-theory broader algebra".
notes: The hierarchical-up relation in a SKOS taxonomy. Inverse of `urn:solid:narrower`. Note: SKOS treats `broader` as transitive only when used inside a single ConceptScheme — for transitive ancestor links, use `skos:broaderTransitive`. For non-hierarchical relatedness, use `urn:solid:related`.

rdfs:label: bto
rdfs:comment: Private primary recipients of the object — "to" addresses hidden from other receivers.
notes: Like `as:to` for delivery, but stripped from the object before any non-`bto` receiver sees it — use for private direct recipients you don't want exposed in the object's metadata. Same caveats as `bcc`: easily leaked by misbehaving intermediaries.

rdfs:label: byteSize
rdfs:comment: The size in bytes of a DCAT Distribution.
notes: Use to declare the file size of a Distribution so consumers can plan downloads. Integer bytes (no "MB"/"GB" suffix — use the raw number). Schema.org's `schema:contentSize` accepts free-form strings; `dcat:byteSize` is stricter.

rdfs:label: cc
rdfs:comment: Secondary public recipients of the object — visible carbon-copy addresses.
notes: Email-style cc: secondary visible recipients. ActivityPub clients typically use `cc` to add a follower collection alongside a primary `to` of `as:Public`, so a post is publicly visible AND fans out to followers' home timelines. Use `as:bcc` to reach recipients privately (not visible in the rendered object).

rdfs:label: changeNote
rdfs:comment: A SKOS note recording a change made to a Concept — typical use is the curator's log of edits to the term over time.
notes: Audit trail in human-readable form: "renamed from X on 2024-06-12", "narrowed scope to exclude Y". Distinct from `historyNote` (broader narrative history of the Concept) and `editorialNote` (working notes for curators). Often appended rather than overwritten.

jsonld.urn:solid:changeNote: 2024-06-12: split applied mathematics into separate concept

rdfs:label: children
rdfs:comment: A child of the person.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:parent`. Despite the plural label "children", schema.org defines this as one-child-per-statement — repeat for multiple children. Sensitive personal data; consider access control before publishing.

rdfs:label: closeMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that two Concepts in different ConceptSchemes are similar enough to be used interchangeably in some applications.
notes: Symmetric but NOT transitive (unlike `exactMatch`) — that's the whole point: chains of close matches don't preserve enough meaning. Use when concepts overlap meaningfully but you wouldn't claim full equivalence.

rdfs:label: closed
rdfs:comment: Indicates that an ActivityStreams Question is closed — no further responses are accepted. The value may be a date-time, a boolean, or an Object describing how it was closed.
notes: Most often a `xsd:dateTime` carrying the close timestamp — clients render "poll ended at …" and stop accepting votes. The boolean form simply marks the Question closed without a time. Some servers also accept an Object value pointing at the activity that closed the poll.

examples.title: A Question with an explicit close time

rdfs:label: conformsTo
rdfs:comment: An established standard or specification to which the resource conforms.
notes: Use to declare specification compliance — e.g. a JSON-LD document conforming to a profile, an HTML page conforming to a WCAG level, a dataset conforming to a schema. Value should be the IRI of the standard, not free text. For shape conformance specifically, see SHACL/ShEx vocabularies.

examples.title: Term file conforming to the urn-solid schema

rdfs:label: contains
rdfs:comment: A resource contained by the LDP Container — i.e., a member created via HTTP POST to the container.
notes: LDP-specific containment with HTTP semantics: POSTing to the container creates a resource that's automatically a `ldp:contains` member. Unlike `urn:solid:hasPart` (a logical part-of), `contains` reflects actual server-side parent-child storage.

rdfs:label: content
rdfs:comment: The textual body of the object — its content in a natural-language string (often HTML).
notes: ActivityStreams' body field. Value is a natural-language string — by convention HTML in ActivityPub, though plain text is allowed. Accompany with `as:mediaType` if not HTML. Repeat with language tags for translations.

rdfs:label: contentMap
rdfs:comment: Language-tagged variants of an ActivityStreams Object's `content` — keys are BCP 47 language tags, values are the localised content (often HTML).
notes: The fediverse's standard mechanism for multi-language posts. Mastodon, Misskey, and most ActivityPub servers populate this when an author tags a post's language. Clients select on locale; server-side translation features (Mastodon "translate") add machine-translated entries here.

urn:solid:contentMap.fr: Je viens de livrer une nouvelle fonctionnalité.

rdfs:label: context
rdfs:comment: The context within which the object exists or to which it relates — typically a conversation thread.
notes: ActivityPub uses `as:context` to group all messages in one conversation under a shared identifier — every reply in a thread carries the same `context` IRI, regardless of `inReplyTo` chains. Distinct from JSON-LD's `@context` (a syntactic keyword). The value is typically the IRI of the root post or a synthetic conversation resource.

rdfs:label: contributor
rdfs:comment: An entity responsible for making contributions to the resource — secondary to the principal creator.
notes: Use for editors, reviewers, translators, co-authors of secondary weight. Repeat for multiple contributors. The principal author goes under `urn:solid:creator` instead. For a richer role-aware contribution model, prefer `prov:wasAttributedTo` paired with a `prov:Role`.

rdfs:label: country-name
rdfs:comment: The country name of an Address — typically as a string.
notes: vCard's country line on an Address — typically a country name string ("United Kingdom") or an ISO 3166-1 country code ("GB"). Schema.org equivalent is `schema:addressCountry`. For a full structured country resource, use `urn:solid:Country`.

rdfs:label: created
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was created.
notes: Use ISO 8601 (`xsd:dateTime` or `xsd:date`) values. Set once at creation and never updated — for last-edit times use `urn:solid:modified`. For provenance-grade timestamps with full PROV semantics, prefer `prov:generatedAtTime`.

examples.title: A document with a creation date

rdfs:label: creator
rdfs:comment: An entity primarily responsible for making the resource.
notes: Use for the principal author or maker. Repeat to list multiple co-creators of equal weight; use `dcterms:contributor` for secondary contributors and `dcterms:publisher` for the entity that issued/distributed the resource.

rdfs:label: credentialStatus
rdfs:comment: A reference to a status mechanism for a VerifiableCredential — e.g. a revocation list — that verifiers consult to check whether the credential is still active.
notes: Distinct from expiration (a static date in the credential). Status is dynamic — the credential is signed once but can be revoked any time after. Common types: `RevocationList2020Status`, `StatusList2021Entry`. Verifiers fetch the referenced status document and check the credential's bit/index.

rdfs:label: credentialSubject
rdfs:comment: The entity that a VerifiableCredential makes claims about — most often an Actor identified by a DID or WebID.
notes: The subject of the claim is not necessarily the *holder* of the credential — a parent might hold a credential about their child, or an organisation might hold one about an employee. Modelled as an Object with whatever properties the claim asserts; multiple subjects are permitted via an array.

rdfs:label: current
rdfs:comment: The page of an ActivityStreams Collection that contains the most recent items — clients seeking "what's new" start here rather than at `first`.
notes: Distinct from `as:first` and `as:last`: `current` is the *live edge* of a Collection that grows over time. For an inbox or a follower list, `current` is where new arrivals appear; older items live further along the chain. Servers without a meaningful "current" notion may omit it.

examples.title: Inbox with a current page pointer

rdfs:label: currentProject
rdfs:comment: A project the person is currently active on.
notes: Repeat to list multiple active projects. Move to `foaf:pastProject` when the person stops being involved. The value can be any resource — typically a `urn:solid:Project` or a `urn:solid:Document` describing the project.

examples.title: Person actively working on a project

rdfs:label: date
rdfs:comment: A point or period of time associated with the resource — generic when more specific date predicates don't apply.
notes: Generic date property — prefer the more specific `urn:solid:created`, `urn:solid:modified`, `dcterms:issued`, `dcterms:available` when the role of the date is known. Useful for legacy data or when the date's role is unclear. ISO 8601 values.

rdfs:label: dateAccepted
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was formally accepted — typically by a publisher, peer reviewer, or governing body.
notes: Common in academic publishing — captures the gap between submission, acceptance, and publication. Pair with `dcterms:dateSubmitted` and `urn:solid:issued`. ISO 8601 date.

rdfs:label: dateCopyrighted
rdfs:comment: The date of a statement of copyright over the resource.
notes: The copyright year, distinct from `urn:solid:dateCreated` (when the work was made) and `urn:solid:issued` (when published). Often the same year as creation but can differ for posthumous publication or transferred rights. ISO 8601 date.

rdfs:label: dateCreated
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was created.
notes: Schema.org's creation timestamp. Functionally equivalent to `dcterms:created` (`urn:solid:created`); pick by namespace flavor — schema.org for SEO-rich JSON-LD on web pages, dcterms for bibliographic/library data.

rdfs:label: dateModified
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was last modified.
notes: Schema.org's modification timestamp — equivalent to `dcterms:modified` (`urn:solid:modified`) and `as:updated` (`urn:solid:updated`). ISO 8601. Pair with `urn:solid:dateCreated` for the create-then-edit lifecycle.

examples.title: Article with creation and modification dates

rdfs:label: datePublished
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was published — when it became publicly available.
notes: Schema.org's publication timestamp — equivalent to `dcterms:issued` (`urn:solid:issued`) and `as:published` (`urn:solid:published`). Distinct from `urn:solid:dateCreated`: an article can be drafted in private (created) and released later (published). ISO 8601.

rdfs:label: dateSubmitted
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was formally submitted — typically to a publisher, conference, or review process.
notes: Pair with `urn:solid:dateAccepted` and `urn:solid:issued` for the full submission → review → publication timeline. Common in academic publishing, grant applications, RFC processes. ISO 8601 date.

rdfs:label: default
rdfs:comment: Marks an Authorization as the default access policy inherited by descendants of a Container.
notes: Value is a Container URI. The Authorization then applies — by inheritance — to every resource inside that Container (recursively) which does not have its own ACL. Replaces the older `acl:defaultForNew`. Without `default`, an Authorization on a Container governs only the Container resource itself, not its members.

examples.title: Authorization that grants Read by default to a subtree

rdfs:label: definition
rdfs:comment: A complete explanation of the intended meaning of a SKOS Concept.
notes: Use a single, dictionary-style sentence per language (multilingual via `@language`). Distinct from `urn:solid:scopeNote` (guidance on how to use the concept) and `urn:solid:description` (general dcterms description).

jsonld.urn:solid:definition: A branch of mathematics that studies abstract structures and their relationships via objects and morphisms.

rdfs:label: deleted
rdfs:comment: On an ActivityStreams Tombstone, the date-time at which the original Object was deleted.
notes: Always an `xsd:dateTime`. Pair with `as:formerType` so consumers know both *when* and *what* was deleted. Together they let UIs render "Note deleted at 14:32" instead of an opaque error when a previously-cached link points to a removed Object.

rdfs:label: depiction
rdfs:comment: An image that depicts the subject.
notes: The value is the IRI of the image itself, not a document containing it. Inverse of `foaf:depicts`. For a profile photo specifically, `vcard:hasPhoto` is often more appropriate in vCard-flavored data.

rdfs:label: describes
rdfs:comment: The Object that an ActivityStreams Profile is about — links a profile-style description to its subject.
notes: Reciprocal of the conceptual "profile of" relationship: a Profile uses `as:describes` to point at the entity it documents. Lets descriptive payloads (long bios, alternate display variants) live as separate, fetchable Objects without polluting the subject's primary record.

rdfs:label: description
rdfs:comment: An account of the resource — a free-text description.
notes: Multi-sentence prose describing what the resource is or contains. For a one-line summary, prefer `rdfs:comment` (which is what RDF tooling usually surfaces); for a tagline, `dcterms:abstract`. Repeat with language tags for translations.

jsonld.urn:solid:description: An introduction to the urn-solid registry and how to use it.

rdfs:label: differentFrom
rdfs:comment: Asserts that two OWL individuals are *not* the same — explicit negation, useful in worlds where the open-world assumption would otherwise leave identity ambiguous.
notes: Symmetric — `A differentFrom B` implies `B differentFrom A`. Distinct from `owl:disjointWith` (which separates *classes*); `differentFrom` separates *individuals*. Necessary because RDF doesn't assume Unique Name Assumption: without `differentFrom`, two distinctly-named resources might still be merged by reasoners.

examples.title: Two people explicitly marked as different

rdfs:label: disjointWith
rdfs:comment: Asserts that two OWL classes have no instances in common — nothing can be both at once.
notes: Symmetric: if A is disjoint with B, B is disjoint with A. Reasoners use this to detect contradictions: declaring an instance as both `Living` and `Deceased` (when those are disjoint) flags the data as inconsistent. Use sparingly — many seemingly-disjoint pairs turn out to overlap in edge cases.

examples.title: Person and Document are disjoint classes

rdfs:label: domain
rdfs:comment: Declares which class an RDF property is meant to be applied to — its subject type.
notes: Subject-side constraint: `acl:agent` has domain `acl:Authorization` because authorisations are what carry it. Multiple domain triples mean the property applies to instances of *all* the listed classes (intersection), not any of them — a common trap.

rdfs:label: downloadURL
rdfs:comment: A direct file URL where a DCAT Distribution can be downloaded.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:accessURL`: `downloadURL` is a *direct* file link (returns the bytes), `accessURL` is any landing page or API entry point. A Distribution typically has one or the other.

rdfs:label: duration
rdfs:comment: How long the object lasts — for time-bounded objects like events, audio, or video.
notes: An `xsd:duration` value (ISO 8601 — e.g. `"PT3M30S"` for 3 minutes 30 seconds). Used on Events, audio/video objects, and any time-bounded thing. For start/end points, use `urn:solid:startTime` and `urn:solid:endTime` instead.

rdfs:label: editor
rdfs:comment: The editor of a CreativeWork — typically a Person who supervised, revised, or curated the content.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:author` (the writer) and `urn:solid:contributor` (general secondary participants): `editor` specifically names the editorial responsibility — the person who shaped, reviewed, or curated the work. Repeat for multiple editors.

rdfs:label: editorialNote
rdfs:comment: A SKOS note for vocabulary maintainers — internal guidance, open questions, things to revisit later. Not intended for end users.
notes: The "TODO" of the SKOS note family — "check whether this should subsume Y", "awaiting decision from working group". Renderers SHOULD hide editorial notes from public displays, surfacing them only in editing UIs.

jsonld.urn:solid:editorialNote: Reconsider scope after the WG ratifies the new taxonomy in Q3.

rdfs:label: educationLevel
rdfs:comment: The general education level the resource targets — primary, secondary, undergraduate, professional, etc.
notes: Used in educational-resources metadata to declare what level of learner the resource is suitable for. Value is typically a controlled-vocabulary term (e.g. from a `schema:DefinedTerm` set) or a free-form string when no controlled vocab applies.

rdfs:label: email
rdfs:comment: An email address for the subject, as a plain string.
notes: Schema.org's simple string-valued email predicate (`"alice@example.org"`). Distinct from `urn:solid:mbox` (FOAF, uses a `mailto:` IRI and is inverse-functional) and `urn:solid:hasEmail` (vCard, typically points at a structured vcard:Email). Use whichever matches your data source.

rdfs:label: endTime
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object ends.
notes: ISO 8601 datetime marking when an Event, Activity, or other time-bounded object ends. Pair with `urn:solid:startTime`. May be omitted for ongoing or open-ended objects. For PROV-grade activity timing, prefer `prov:endedAtTime`.

rdfs:label: endedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which the activity ended.
notes: PROV-grade activity-end timestamp. Pair with `urn:solid:startedAtTime` to record execution windows. May be omitted for ongoing activities. ActivityStreams `urn:solid:endTime` is the equivalent for AS Events; pick by domain — PROV for processes, AS for calendar events.

examples.title: Build with start and end timestamps

rdfs:label: endpointDescription
rdfs:comment: A machine-readable description of how to interact with a DCAT DataService — e.g. an OpenAPI document or SPARQL Service Description.
notes: `endpointURL` is *where* to call; `endpointDescription` is *how* to call it. Common values: a SPARQL 1.1 Service Description graph, an OpenAPI/Swagger JSON document, a Hydra ApiDocumentation. Without a description, clients must rely on out-of-band knowledge of the protocol.

examples.title: Service with a SPARQL service description

rdfs:label: endpointURL
rdfs:comment: The root URL of a DCAT DataService — the address a client connects to to invoke the service.
notes: Names the operational entry point. For a SPARQL endpoint, the query URL; for a REST API, the base URI. Pair with `dcat:endpointDescription` (a machine-readable description of how to talk to it — OpenAPI doc, SPARQL service description) when the service is non-trivial.

rdfs:label: endpoints
rdfs:comment: Container for additional service endpoints exposed by an ActivityPub Actor — most importantly `sharedInbox`, but also `proxyUrl`, OAuth endpoints, and others.
notes: Value is an Object whose properties are well-known endpoint names. The most-used in practice is `sharedInbox` (a single inbox URL serving multiple Actors on the same server, used to deduplicate fan-out). Federated servers SHOULD prefer `endpoints.sharedInbox` over per-Actor `inbox` when delivering the same Activity to many local recipients.

rdfs:label: equivalentClass
rdfs:comment: Asserts that two OWL classes have identical extensions — every instance of one is also an instance of the other and vice versa.
notes: Stronger than mutual `subClassOf` — `equivalentClass` is two-way subclass, but as a single assertion it makes the equivalence explicit for reasoners. Distinct from `owl:sameAs`, which equates *individuals*. Use to bridge two parallel class hierarchies (e.g. `foaf:Person` and `schema:Person`).

rdfs:label: equivalentProperty
rdfs:comment: Asserts that two OWL properties always relate the same subjects to the same objects — interchangeable in any triple.
notes: Property analogue of `owl:equivalentClass`. Stronger than mutual `subPropertyOf`. Use to bridge identical predicates across vocabularies — `foaf:name` and `schema:name` are commonly equated this way for cross-vocab interop.

rdfs:label: exactMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that two Concepts in different ConceptSchemes are equivalent for retrieval purposes.
notes: Symmetric and transitive — assert sparingly because chains can produce surprising equivalences across vocabularies. For weaker similarity that doesn't claim full equivalence, prefer `urn:solid:closeMatch`. Use across SKOS schemes; within one scheme, use `urn:solid:broader`/`narrower`/`related` instead.

rdfs:label: example
rdfs:comment: An example illustrating the use of a SKOS Concept.
notes: Editorial property for cataloguers — provides a sample use of the concept. Repeat for multiple examples. Mirrors the per-term `examples` arrays on urn-solid term files (which are JSON-LD snippets, while `skos:example` is plain prose).

jsonld.urn:solid:example: The List monad in Haskell — sequences with bind/return.

rdfs:label: expirationDate
rdfs:comment: The date-time at which a VerifiableCredential ceases to be valid — verifiers SHOULD reject it after this instant.
notes: Optional — credentials without an expiration are open-ended. VC 2.0 renames this to `validUntil`; both are seen in the wild. Distinct from revocation: expiration is set at issuance and absolute; revocation is dynamic and consulted via `credentialStatus`.

examples.title: A credential valid for one year

rdfs:label: extent
rdfs:comment: The size or duration of the resource — pages, bytes, runtime length.
notes: Free-form size/duration string in dcterms tradition ("320 pages", "45 minutes", "2.4 MB"). For machine-readable durations specifically, prefer `urn:solid:duration` (xsd:duration). For byte counts, use `schema:contentSize` directly.

rdfs:label: family-name
rdfs:comment: The vCard family name (surname) of a person.
notes: vCard's hyphenated form of the family name — distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:familyName` (camelCase) only by namespace. Pick `family-name` in vCard-flavored data, `familyName` in FOAF/schema-flavored data. Functionally equivalent.

rdfs:label: familyName
rdfs:comment: The family name (surname) of the person.
notes: Modern preferred form (the older `foaf:family_name` and `foaf:surname` are seen too — kept under `rdfs:seeAlso`). Pair with `foaf:givenName` for structured names. Use `urn:solid:name` for a single combined display name.

rdfs:label: first
rdfs:comment: The first page of a paginated ActivityStreams Collection — the entry point a client uses to start walking the pagination chain.
notes: On a Collection that is too large to inline, `as:first` points at a CollectionPage which can be followed via `next` (and optionally back via `prev`). For ordered collections (`as:OrderedCollection`), `first` is the chronologically/structurally earliest page; for unordered, the order is server-defined.

rdfs:label: firstName
rdfs:comment: The first name of a person.
notes: Older sibling of `foaf:givenName` — kept for compatibility with legacy FOAF data. New profiles should prefer `foaf:givenName` (modeled as `urn:solid:givenName` once added) and `foaf:familyName`. The semantic distinction between first/given is culture-bound; treat them as equivalent in practice.

rdfs:label: fn
rdfs:comment: Formatted name — the display name of the subject as a single string.
notes: vCard's canonical display-name property — carries the full formatted form ("Alice Liddell"), not the structured given/family fields. `urn:solid:name` is FOAF's equivalent; prefer it for non-vCard data. For structured names, use `urn:solid:givenName` + `urn:solid:familyName`.

rdfs:label: follower
rdfs:comment: An agent that follows the subject — receiving updates from them.
notes: Schema.org's reverse follower relation (their `schema:follows` is symmetric in the spec but typically used as inverse of `schema:follows`). For ActivityPub, the typical pattern is an `as:Followers` Collection at `as:followers` on the subject; for this lightweight schema.org form, just enumerate followers directly.

rdfs:label: followers
rdfs:comment: The Collection of Actors who follow an ActivityPub Actor — used both for delivery (servers fan Activities out to followers) and for display.
notes: The Actor's audience — addressed as `as:to: <followers-uri>` in many activities to broadcast to the Collection without enumerating each follower. Servers may keep this Collection private (returning only `totalItems`) for privacy. Inverse direction is `as:following`.

examples.title: An Actor exposing a followers Collection

rdfs:label: following
rdfs:comment: The Collection of Actors that an ActivityPub Actor follows — the source side of the social graph.
notes: Mirror of `as:followers`. Each entry is an Actor whose Activities the subject has subscribed to via a `Follow` activity. May be private (just a count) for privacy-sensitive deployments.

examples.title: An Actor exposing a following Collection

rdfs:label: forClass
rdfs:comment: The RDF class that a TypeRegistration is for — what type of resources live at the registered location.
notes: The discriminator for TypeIndex lookups: when an app wants to know "where do this user's photos live?", it scans the TypeIndex for a registration whose `forClass` matches the relevant class IRI (e.g. `foaf:Image`).

rdfs:label: format
rdfs:comment: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource.
notes: Use an IANA media type string (`text/html`, `application/ld+json`, `image/png`) for digital resources. For physical media or non-MIME formats, free-form descriptive text is acceptable. Range can also be a `dcterms:MediaType` resource for richer modelling.

rdfs:label: formerType
rdfs:comment: On an ActivityStreams Tombstone, the type the deleted Object had before it was removed — preserves enough metadata for clients to know what they lost.
notes: After deletion, the Tombstone replaces the original Object at its URL. `as:formerType` records what `@type` it used to have (a `Note`, an `Image`, an `Article`); `as:deleted` records when. Together they let renderers display "a deleted Note" rather than just an opaque hole.

examples.title: A Tombstone for a deleted Note

rdfs:label: gender
rdfs:comment: The gender of the agent — a free-form string in FOAF tradition.
notes: Privacy-sensitive. FOAF intentionally uses a free-form string rather than an enumerated type so identity can be self-described. `schema:gender` accepts either a `GenderType` (enum) or a string; `vcard:hasGender` uses an enumerated controlled vocabulary. Use whichever matches the consumer.

rdfs:label: generated
rdfs:comment: Inverse of `prov:wasGeneratedBy` — the Entity that this Activity produced.
notes: Convenient when describing the world from the Activity's perspective ("what did this run produce?"). Either direction is valid; pick whichever makes the focal entity the subject. Pair with `prov:used` (inputs) and `prov:invalidated` (entities the Activity consumed/destroyed).

rdfs:label: generatedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which the entity was completely generated by some activity.
notes: PROV's precise generation timestamp — paired with `prov:wasGeneratedBy` it lets you record exactly when a build, run, or process completed. Use `urn:solid:created` for lightweight "when was this resource made" without the PROV ceremony.

rdfs:label: generator
rdfs:comment: The application that generated the object — typically a software client or service.
notes: ActivityStreams' "created with" attribution — the value is the client app (e.g. a Mastodon instance, a Solid app). Distinct from `urn:solid:wasGeneratedBy` (PROV-grade activity attribution): generator names *what software*, wasGeneratedBy names *what process run*.

examples.title: Note generated by a client app

rdfs:label: given-name
rdfs:comment: The vCard given name (first name) of a person.
notes: vCard's hyphenated form of the given name — distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:givenName` (camelCase) only by namespace. Pick `given-name` in vCard-flavored data, `givenName` in FOAF/schema-flavored data. Functionally equivalent.

rdfs:label: givenName
rdfs:comment: The given name of a person — the personal name distinct from the family name.
notes: Modern preferred form for the personal/first name component. Pair with `urn:solid:familyName` for structured names. The older `foaf:firstName` is treated as equivalent in most consumers; prefer `givenName` for new data.

rdfs:label: hadActivity
rdfs:comment: An activity that contributed to a qualified PROV relation — typically attached to a qualified usage, generation, or derivation.
notes: Used inside qualified PROV relations (`prov:qualifiedDerivation`, `prov:qualifiedUsage`, `prov:qualifiedGeneration`) to name the specific Activity that mediated the relation. Lets you attach a Plan, Role, or timing to the connection.

examples.title: Derivation referencing the activity that produced it

rdfs:label: hadGeneration
rdfs:comment: Links a use of an Entity to the qualified Generation event in which that Entity was created — letting consumers reason about which version was used.
notes: Used inside qualified PROV patterns — e.g. on a `prov:Usage` instance, `prov:hadGeneration` points to the `prov:Generation` of the entity that was used. Pairs naturally with `prov:hadActivity` to fully reconstruct the lineage of a specific use.

examples.title: Qualified Usage citing the source Generation

rdfs:label: hadMember
rdfs:comment: An entity that was a member of a PROV Collection.
notes: PROV's collection-membership predicate (`prov:Collection` is distinct from `as:Collection` and `ldp:Container`). Use only in PROV-flavored contexts; for FOAF Group membership use `urn:solid:member`, for vCard Group use `urn:solid:hasMember`, for LDP containers use `urn:solid:contains`.

rdfs:label: hadPlan
rdfs:comment: The Plan that an Activity followed — used inside a qualified PROV Association.
notes: Used inside a `prov:Association` to point at the `urn:solid:Plan` the Agent followed when participating in the Activity. Lets PROV record "who acted, with what role, following which plan" — a build run executes a build plan; a paper review follows a review checklist.

rdfs:label: hadPrimarySource
rdfs:comment: An entity that is the primary source — the original first-hand source — for the subject entity.
notes: PROV's primary-source predicate, a specialization of `prov:wasDerivedFrom`. "Primary source" means original/first-hand — the eyewitness account, the raw measurement, the canonical document. For derivations more generally (translations, summaries, transformed datasets), `urn:solid:wasDerivedFrom` is broader.

examples.title: News article with a primary source

rdfs:label: hadRole
rdfs:comment: The role an Agent or Entity played in a qualified PROV relation — "author", "editor", "raw input", etc.
notes: Used inside qualified PROV relations to name the role taken. Distinct from `urn:solid:role` (vCard's job-title string): `hadRole` is specifically about role within an Activity or Attribution. Value is typically a `prov:Role` resource (which can be any IRI).

rdfs:label: hadUsage
rdfs:comment: Inside a qualified PROV pattern, links to the `prov:Usage` event whose entity participated in this relationship — typically used on a `prov:Derivation` to record the use that supplied its input.
notes: A connector between qualified PROV events. On a `prov:Derivation`, `prov:hadUsage` points at the `prov:Usage` of the input entity by the activity, and `prov:hadGeneration` points at the `prov:Generation` of the output. Together they reconstruct the precise link between two entities through an activity.

examples.title: Derivation citing the Usage of its source

rdfs:label: hasAddress
rdfs:comment: A postal address associated with the subject.
notes: The value should be a `vcard:Address` (or `schema:PostalAddress`) resource carrying structured fields — `vcard:street-address`, `vcard:locality`, `vcard:postal-code`, `vcard:country-name`. For an approximate "based near" location, use `urn:solid:basedNear` instead.

rdfs:label: hasCalendarBusy
rdfs:comment: A URL of the subject's free/busy calendar — shows availability without exposing event details.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:hasCalendarLink` (full calendar with event details). Use for a privacy-preserving free/busy feed — schedulers can find open slots without seeing what's on. Typically a CalDAV free-busy URL or .ifb file.

rdfs:label: hasCalendarLink
rdfs:comment: A URL of the subject's calendar — typically an iCalendar (.ics) feed or web calendar.
notes: Use to point at a public calendar — an .ics URL, a CalDAV endpoint, or a calendar page. For subscriber-friendly links, use a `webcal:` URI; for plain HTTPS, the consumer must know how to subscribe. Distinct from `urn:solid:hasCalendarBusy` (free/busy availability only).

rdfs:label: hasCalendarRequest
rdfs:comment: A vCard's URL for accepting calendar requests — the endpoint where meeting requests, scheduling proposals, or iCalendar invitations should be sent.
notes: vCard analogue of the iCalendar CALADRURI property. Distinct from `vcard:hasCalendarLink` (a public calendar URL to *view*) and `vcard:hasCalendarBusy` (free/busy lookup) — `hasCalendarRequest` is specifically the *write* endpoint for inbound scheduling.

examples.title: A VCard exposing a scheduling endpoint

rdfs:label: hasCategory
rdfs:comment: A category or tag for the vCard — describing what kind of contact it is.
notes: vCard's category/tag predicate — typical values are "work", "personal", "family", "friend". Repeat for multiple categories. For general-purpose tagging of resources (not specifically vCards), prefer `urn:solid:keywords` or `urn:solid:subject`.

examples.title: vCard categorized as a work contact

rdfs:label: hasEmail
rdfs:comment: An email address associated with the subject — typically a `mailto:` IRI.
notes: vCard's general email predicate: not inverse-functional and free of FOAF's strong identity semantics. Use `urn:solid:mbox` when the email uniquely identifies the agent (FOAF tradition). Multiple `hasEmail` values are typical (work, personal, etc.).

rdfs:label: hasFormat
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is the same intellectual content but in a different format — e.g. a PDF version of an HTML article.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:hasVersion`: same content, different file format (PDF vs HTML, MP3 vs FLAC, JSON-LD vs Turtle). Inverse is `dcterms:isFormatOf`. The format itself is described by `urn:solid:format`.

examples.title: Article available in PDF and HTML

rdfs:label: hasGender
rdfs:comment: The gender of the agent — typically referencing one of vCard's enumerated Gender values.
notes: vCard's typed gender predicate, distinct from FOAF `urn:solid:gender` (free-form string). Value is typically a `vcard:Male`, `vcard:Female`, `vcard:Other`, `vcard:None`, or a custom resource. Privacy-sensitive — collect only when needed.

rdfs:label: hasGeo
rdfs:comment: Geographic coordinates associated with the subject — typically a `geo:` IRI carrying lat/long.
notes: Use a `geo:` URI (e.g. `geo:51.5074,-0.1278`) for the value. For richer coordinate modelling with separate lat/long predicates, use `schema:GeoCoordinates` or the WGS84 `geo:` ontology.

rdfs:label: hasInstantMessage
rdfs:comment: An instant-messaging address for the subject — typically an `xmpp:`, `matrix:`, or other chat URI.
notes: vCard's general IM-address slot — covers any chat protocol via URI scheme (`xmpp:`, `matrix:`, `irc:`). Distinct from FOAF's `urn:solid:jabberID` which is XMPP-specific and a bare string. Repeat for multiple IM identities.

rdfs:label: hasKey
rdfs:comment: A cryptographic public key associated with the vCard's owner — for encryption or signature verification.
notes: vCard's lightweight public-key pointer. Value is typically a URL of the key file (PGP, SSH, X.509). For richer key metadata (algorithm, usage, controllers), use the W3C Security Vocabulary. Repeat for multiple keys (encryption, signing, etc.).

examples.title: vCard with a PGP key URL

rdfs:label: hasLanguage
rdfs:comment: A language the subject communicates in — typically a BCP 47 language tag.
notes: vCard's communicates-in-language predicate. Functionally similar to schema's `urn:solid:knowsLanguage`; pick whichever matches your data flavor. Distinct from `urn:solid:language` (the language a *resource* is in). Value is typically a BCP 47 tag.

rdfs:label: hasLogo
rdfs:comment: A logo image associated with the vCard — typically the brand mark of an Organization.
notes: Use on Organization vCards for the brand mark. Distinct from `urn:solid:hasPhoto` (typically a person's portrait). Schema.org's equivalent is `schema:logo`. Value can be a URL or a `urn:solid:Logo` resource.

rdfs:label: hasMember
rdfs:comment: A member of the vCard Group.
notes: vCard's group-membership predicate. Distinct from `urn:solid:member` (FOAF) only by namespace; functionally the same. Use `hasMember` in vCard-flavored data, `member` in FOAF-flavored data. Repeat for multiple members.

rdfs:label: hasMemberRelation
rdfs:comment: The predicate that should be used to express membership in a DirectContainer or IndirectContainer.
notes: Used on a `DirectContainer` or `IndirectContainer` to declare which predicate the server should add when a new resource is POSTed — e.g. `schema:comment` so a new POST to a comments container produces `<post> schema:comment <new-comment>`. Alternative: `ldp:isMemberOfRelation` for the inverse direction.

examples.title: Comments container declaring its member relation

rdfs:label: hasName
rdfs:comment: A structured Name resource for the subject — separates given/family/additional/prefix/suffix into a Name object.
notes: Use when name parts need to live on a separate Name resource (e.g. for multi-script names or when the parts have their own metadata). Most data instead attaches `given-name`/`family-name`/etc. directly to the VCard. The flat-string form is `urn:solid:fn`.

rdfs:label: hasNickname
rdfs:comment: A nickname for the subject.
notes: vCard's nickname predicate — the structured equivalent of FOAF's `urn:solid:nick`. Pick `hasNickname` in vCard-flavored data, `nick` in FOAF-flavored data. Repeat for multiple nicknames.

rdfs:label: hasPart
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is included as a part of the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:isPartOf`. Use to enumerate the constituent parts of a compound resource (chapters of a book, articles in a journal issue, photos in an album). Repeat for multiple parts.

rdfs:label: hasPhoto
rdfs:comment: A photo associated with the subject — typically a portrait.
notes: vCard's photo predicate. Functionally similar to `urn:solid:img`; pick `hasPhoto` in vCard-flavored data and `img`/`depiction` in FOAF-flavored data. Multiple values are typical (gallery, alternates, sizes).

rdfs:label: hasRelated
rdfs:comment: A related contact for the vCard — typically another person (spouse, child, colleague) connected to the subject.
notes: vCard's general inter-contact relation. Pair with `vcard:hasRelatedType` (work-colleague, family, etc.) for typed relations. Distinct from SKOS `urn:solid:related` (between Concepts) and from FOAF `urn:solid:knows` (between Persons in a social-graph sense).

examples.title: vCard pointing at a related contact

rdfs:label: hasSound
rdfs:comment: A vCard's URL pointing at an audio recording — typically a pronunciation of the name or a personal voice intro.
notes: Carried over from RFC 6350 (vCard 4.0) — primarily used for name-pronunciation clips so callers say the name correctly. Niche today; mainstream contact apps mostly ignore it. Modern equivalent is a Profile-attached `as:Audio` Object.

examples.title: A VCard with a pronunciation recording

rdfs:label: hasSource
rdfs:comment: A source document for the vCard's information — typically a website or directory the data came from.
notes: vCard-specific source pointer — analogous to `dcterms:source` (`urn:solid:source`) but scoped to vCards and typed for the directory-import scenario. Useful when a contact card was scraped or auto-imported and you want to record the upstream URL.

rdfs:label: hasSubOrganization
rdfs:comment: An OrganizationalUnit (department, team, division) that is part of the parent Organization.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:subOrganizationOf`. Use to enumerate departments/units belonging to a parent. Repeat for multiple subunits.

examples.title: Company with engineering and sales units

rdfs:label: hasTelephone
rdfs:comment: A telephone number associated with the subject — typically a `tel:` IRI.
notes: Use a `tel:` URI (e.g. `tel:+44-20-1234-5678`) for the value, not a bare string. Repeat for multiple numbers. For typed numbers (work/home/mobile), the value can be a `vcard:Tel` resource carrying `vcard:hasValue` and `rdf:type` of one of the work/home/cell sub-types.

rdfs:label: hasTopConcept
rdfs:comment: A top-level (root) Concept of the SKOS ConceptScheme — has no broader concept within the scheme.
notes: Use on a ConceptScheme to enumerate its entry-point Concepts — those with no `broader` parent in the scheme. Inverse is `urn:solid:topConceptOf`. A scheme typically has a small handful of top concepts; repeat for each.

rdfs:label: hasUID
rdfs:comment: A globally unique identifier for the vCard — typically a UUID or other long-lived ID.
notes: vCard's persistent identifier — the value remains stable across edits, lets clients dedupe two card revisions for the same person. Often a `urn:uuid:`. Distinct from `urn:solid:identifier` (general-purpose secondary identifier); `hasUID` is specifically the vCard tradition's stable ID.

rdfs:label: hasURL
rdfs:comment: A URL associated with the subject — any web link, not necessarily the canonical homepage.
notes: More general than `urn:solid:homepage` — use to enumerate any URLs (social profiles, project links, work pages). Repeat for multiple. Use `homepage` when the URL is the canonical, FOAF-style identifying homepage.

rdfs:label: hasUnit
rdfs:comment: An OrganizationalUnit that is part of the parent Organization — narrower than `hasSubOrganization`.
notes: Sub-property of `urn:solid:hasSubOrganization` constrained to OrganizationalUnits (so the value is always an internal unit, not another formal organization). Use when you want type-checking on the structure.

rdfs:label: hasVersion
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is a version, edition, or adaptation of the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:isVersionOf`. Use on the abstract work to enumerate its versions/editions. Repeat for multiple versions; useful for spec families, software releases, document editions.

rdfs:label: headline
rdfs:comment: The headline of the article — a short, attention-grabbing title line.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:name` — the headline is specifically the newsroom-style top line of an article ("Local CG Founder Ships Registry"), while `name` is the generic title. Keep headlines concise (schema.org recommends ≤ 110 characters).

rdfs:label: height
rdfs:comment: The height in pixels of an ActivityStreams Object — typically an Image, Video, or Link to a visual resource.
notes: In pixels, not CSS units. Pair with `as:width` so renderers can reserve layout space and avoid reflow when the image loads. For multi-resolution variants, expose each as a distinct Link with its own height/width and let clients pick.

rdfs:label: heldBy
rdfs:comment: Inverse of `org:holds` — names the Agent currently filling an organizational Post.
notes: Convenient for queries that start at a Post ("who is the CTO?"). For time-bounded historical assertions, model the relationship as a `org:Membership` instead — `heldBy` is a snapshot, not a record.

examples.title: A Post and its current holder

rdfs:label: hiddenLabel
rdfs:comment: A non-display label for a SKOS Concept — used to support search but not shown in UIs.
notes: Use for misspellings, deprecated names, slang — strings users might search for that you don't want to surface in the UI. SKOS rule: `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, and `hiddenLabel` values must be pairwise disjoint within a language for the same Concept.

rdfs:label: historyNote
rdfs:comment: A SKOS note describing the history of a Concept — its origin, evolution, and how its meaning has shifted over time.
notes: Narrative rather than transactional: where the term came from, why it exists, how usage has changed. Distinct from `changeNote` (specific edit log) and `editorialNote` (curator working notes). Public-facing — useful in glossaries and documentation pages.

jsonld.urn:solid:historyNote: Coined by Norbert Wiener in 1948; usage broadened through the 1960s to cover any feedback-driven system.

rdfs:label: holder
rdfs:comment: On a VerifiablePresentation, the Actor presenting the credentials — typically (but not always) also the credentialSubject.
notes: Three roles in a typical VC flow: `issuer` (signs the credential), `credentialSubject` (the entity it makes claims about), `holder` (the entity presenting it now). They're often the same Actor but can diverge — a parent holding a credential about their child, an organisation holding one about an employee.

examples.title: A presentation with an explicit holder

rdfs:label: holds
rdfs:comment: An ORG Post (position) that an Agent currently holds within an Organization.
notes: Use to declare that a Person currently occupies a named Post (org:Post) — "holds the position of CTO". A Post is a stable, identified position that may be held by different people over time, distinct from Membership (which is the participation event itself).

rdfs:label: homepage
rdfs:comment: A homepage for the subject — a top-level page about the agent.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF: a homepage uniquely identifies its agent. Use the IRI of the actual page, not a description of it. For arbitrary URLs that are not the canonical homepage, prefer `schema:url` or `vcard:hasURL`.

rdfs:label: honorific-prefix
rdfs:comment: An honorific prefix preceding the person's name — Mr, Mrs, Dr, Prof, etc.
notes: vCard's honorific prefix — culture-specific. Pair with `urn:solid:honorific-suffix` for postnominals (PhD, Esq.). Schema.org equivalent is `schema:honorificPrefix`. Note the hyphen in the source name is preserved.

rdfs:label: honorific-suffix
rdfs:comment: An honorific suffix following the person's name — PhD, Esq, Jr, Sr, etc.
notes: vCard's postnominal field — degrees, generational suffixes, certifications. Pair with `urn:solid:honorific-prefix`. Schema.org equivalent is `schema:honorificSuffix`. Repeat for multiple postnominals ("PhD, FRS").

rdfs:label: href
rdfs:comment: The target URL of an ActivityStreams Link — the resource the Link points at.
notes: The defining property of a Link — without `href` a Link has no destination. Distinct from `@id` (the Link object's own identifier, often omitted): `@id` identifies the Link, `href` identifies what it links to. Used heavily by `Mention` and `Hashtag` to point at the mentioned actor or topic feed.

examples.title: A Link with href and rel

rdfs:label: hreflang
rdfs:comment: The language of the resource at an ActivityStreams Link's `href` — a BCP 47 language tag (`en`, `en-GB`, `pt-BR`).
notes: Lets clients pick the right localisation when a Link offers translations. Pair with `as:rel: alternate` and a separate Link per language so consumers can choose. Mirrors HTML's `<a hreflang>` and Atom's `link/@hreflang`.

rdfs:label: icon
rdfs:comment: A small image representing the object — typically a square avatar or favicon.
notes: ActivityStreams' small-avatar slot — typically square, low-resolution, used as the visual identifier for an actor or object in lists. The value is an Image or a URL. For a full-size portrait, prefer `urn:solid:img` (FOAF) or `urn:solid:depiction`.

rdfs:label: identifier
rdfs:comment: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.
notes: Use for non-URI identifiers (DOI strings, ISBN, internal IDs, UUIDs) where the resource also has a URI as its `@id`. The resource's primary identifier is its `@id`; this property records additional/secondary identifiers. Repeat to list multiple.

rdfs:label: img
rdfs:comment: An image that represents the person — typically a headshot or portrait.
notes: A sub-property of `foaf:depiction` specifically for a portrait of a person. Prefer `urn:solid:depiction` when the subject is any kind of thing or the image is not a portrait. A person may have at most one primary `img` but multiple `depiction` values.

rdfs:label: inDataset
rdfs:comment: Links a DCAT Distribution to the Dataset it represents — inverse of `dcat:distribution`.
notes: Convenient when the data flow starts at a Distribution (e.g. "what dataset is this CSV part of?"). Either direction is valid; use `dcat:distribution` (Dataset → Distribution) when the Dataset is the focal entity, `dcat:inDataset` (Distribution → Dataset) when the Distribution is.

examples.title: A Distribution pointing back at its Dataset

rdfs:label: inLanguage
rdfs:comment: The language a CreativeWork is written in — typically a BCP 47 language tag.
notes: Schema.org's resource-language predicate. Functionally equivalent to dcterms `urn:solid:language` — pick by namespace flavor (schema for SEO, dcterms for bibliographic). Distinct from `urn:solid:knowsLanguage` (an Agent's languages).

rdfs:label: inReplyTo
rdfs:comment: An object the current object is a reply to.
notes: Use to link a reply Note (or other object) back at its parent. Forms reply threads in ActivityPub. Repeat for replies addressing multiple parents (rare). The inverse `as:replies` lives on the parent and points at a Collection of replies.

examples.title: Reply pointing at its parent note

rdfs:label: inScheme
rdfs:comment: The SKOS ConceptScheme that the Concept is a member of.
notes: Declares membership of a Concept in a ConceptScheme. A Concept may belong to multiple schemes — repeat for each. The transitive scope of `broader`/`narrower` is bounded by `inScheme` membership.

examples.title: Concept belonging to a topic taxonomy

rdfs:label: inbox
rdfs:comment: An LDN inbox — a container that accepts notifications about the resource via HTTP POST.
notes: From Linked Data Notifications (LDN). The value is a Container that accepts incoming notifications about the subject — anyone can POST to it to leave a notification (subject to access control). ActivityPub re-uses the concept under `as:inbox` (a separate but interoperable IRI).

rdfs:label: insertedContentRelation
rdfs:comment: On an IndirectContainer, the predicate the server uses to look up the actual member from the POSTed content.
notes: Used only on `urn:solid:IndirectContainer`. Tells the server: "when a resource is POSTed, look up the value of *this* predicate inside it, and use *that* as the actual member." Common pattern: an IndirectContainer for likes uses `as:actor` so the membership target is the liker, not the Like activity itself.

rdfs:label: instance
rdfs:comment: A single resource that's an instance of the class declared by the TypeRegistration.
notes: Use when the user has exactly one instance — typically a settings document or singleton. For collections of instances under a directory, use `solid:instanceContainer` instead. A single TypeRegistration may carry multiple `solid:instance` values.

examples.title: Registration for a single preferences file

rdfs:label: instanceContainer
rdfs:comment: A Container holding instances of the class declared by a TypeRegistration.
notes: Use when the user's data of a given type lives in a directory that may hold many resources (photos in `/photos/`, notes in `/notes/`). Distinct from `urn:solid:instance`, which points at a single resource. A TypeRegistration uses one or the other, not both.

rdfs:label: instructionalMethod
rdfs:comment: A process used to engender knowledge, attitudes, or skills using the resource — pedagogy.
notes: Used in educational-resources metadata to describe the teaching method (lecture, problem-set, workshop, MOOC video). Value is typically a controlled-vocabulary term or free-form string. Pair with `urn:solid:educationLevel`.

rdfs:label: instrument
rdfs:comment: An entity used by an ActivityStreams Activity to perform its action — e.g. a tool, a client application, or a means by which the Activity was carried out.
notes: Captures the *means* used (a microphone for a Listen, a camera for a View, a client app for a Create). Distinct from `as:object` (what was acted on) and `as:target` (where the action was directed). Often left implicit — populate when the instrument is itself a first-class entity worth referencing.

examples.title: A Listen activity with an instrument

rdfs:label: interest
rdfs:comment: A page about a topic of interest to the agent.
notes: The value is a page (document) representing the topic of interest, not the topic itself. For the topic resource directly (any Thing, not necessarily a Document), use `foaf:topic_interest`. Repeat to list multiple interests.

examples.title: Person interested in a Wikipedia topic

rdfs:label: invalidated
rdfs:comment: An Entity that this PROV Activity destroyed, consumed, or rendered unusable — after invalidation the Entity is no longer available for further use.
notes: Models destruction or consumption explicitly: a delete operation invalidates a record, a publish step invalidates a draft. Distinct from `prov:used` (read without altering) and `prov:generated` (created). Useful in audit trails and data lifecycle tracking.

rdfs:label: invalidatedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which an Entity ceased to exist.
notes: End-of-life timestamp counterpart to `urn:solid:generatedAtTime`. Records when an Entity was deleted, retracted, expired, or otherwise ceased to exist. ISO 8601. Pair with `urn:solid:wasInvalidatedBy` for the responsible Activity.

rdfs:label: inverseOf
rdfs:comment: Asserts that two OWL properties are inverses — `A p1 B` if and only if `B p2 A`.
notes: Reasoners use this to materialise the reverse direction without storing both. Classic pairs: `as:followers` / `as:following`, `dcterms:isPartOf` / `dcterms:hasPart`, `prov:wasGeneratedBy` / `prov:generated`. Symmetric properties (`owl:sameAs`, `foaf:knows`) are their own inverse.

rdfs:label: isDefinedBy
rdfs:comment: Points at the resource that *defines* a term — typically the vocabulary document the term was minted in.
notes: A subproperty of `rdfs:seeAlso` with a stronger claim: the target is *the source of truth* for what the term means, not just related. Each `urn:solid:*` term in this registry could (and arguably should) point at `https://urn-solid.github.io/<Name>/` via `isDefinedBy`.

examples.title: A term pointing at its definition

rdfs:label: isFormatOf
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is the same intellectual content of which the described resource is a different-format rendition.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasFormat`. Use on the alternate-format rendition to point at the canonical resource it represents in another format. Distinct from `isVersionOf` (different version/edition, not just different format).

rdfs:label: isMemberOfRelation
rdfs:comment: The predicate the server adds in the *inverse* direction when a new resource is POSTed to a DirectContainer or IndirectContainer.
notes: Inverse-direction equivalent of `ldp:hasMemberRelation`: instead of `<membershipResource> <pred> <new>`, the server adds `<new> <pred> <membershipResource>`. Use whichever direction matches your data model. A container declares one of `hasMemberRelation` or `isMemberOfRelation`, not both.

rdfs:label: isPartOf
rdfs:comment: A related resource of which the described resource is a part.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasPart`. Use to point at the containing resource (the book a chapter belongs to, the journal an article appears in). One value per containing whole; repeat only if the resource genuinely belongs to multiple containers.

rdfs:label: isPrimaryTopicOf
rdfs:comment: A document of which the subject is the primary topic — the inverse of `primaryTopic`.
notes: Use on a Person (or other thing) to point at the document that primarily describes them. The canonical case is a WebID: `<#me> foaf:isPrimaryTopicOf <profile-card>`. Inverse-functional in FOAF — the document uniquely identifies the subject, and vice versa.

examples.title: Person pointing to their profile document

rdfs:label: isReferencedBy
rdfs:comment: A related resource that references, cites, or otherwise points to the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:references`. Use to enumerate the inbound citations or backlinks to this resource. Repeat for multiple. Often computed by aggregators rather than asserted by the resource itself.

rdfs:label: isReplacedBy
rdfs:comment: A related resource that supplants, displaces, or supersedes the described resource.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:replaces`. Use on the older resource to point at its successor — readers can follow the chain to the current version. The schema's `supersededBy` field on a urn-solid term file is the registry-internal equivalent.

examples.title: v1 spec pointing at its successor

rdfs:label: isRequiredBy
rdfs:comment: A related resource that requires the described resource to support its function or coherence.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:requires`. Use on a dependency to enumerate downstream consumers — "this library is required by these projects". Often computed by package indexes rather than asserted by the resource itself.

examples.title: Library showing what depends on it

rdfs:label: isVersionOf
rdfs:comment: A related resource of which the described resource is a version, edition, or adaptation.
notes: Use to point at the abstract "work" the current resource is one version of. Distinct from `urn:solid:replaces` (which says "this supersedes that"); `isVersionOf` allows multiple concurrent versions of the same work without one displacing another.

examples.title: v2 spec is a version of the spec series

rdfs:label: issuanceDate
rdfs:comment: The date-time at which a VerifiableCredential was issued — the credential is not considered valid before this instant.
notes: Distinct from `dcterms:created` and `dcterms:issued` — `issuanceDate` carries the same semantics but lives in the VC namespace so verifiers and standard libraries find it where they expect. Required on every VC. Note: VC 2.0 renames this to `validFrom`; both forms are seen in the wild.

rdfs:label: issued
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was formally issued or published.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:created` (which is when the resource itself was made) — `issued` is when it was made publicly available. For an article drafted in private and published later, the two diverge. ISO 8601 values.

rdfs:label: issuer
rdfs:comment: The Actor that issued a VerifiableCredential — the party whose key signed the cryptographic proof and whose authority backs the claim.
notes: Either a string IRI or an Object carrying additional issuer metadata (name, image, URL). The issuer's public key — discoverable from this IRI — is what the credential's `proof` is verified against. Without a resolvable issuer, a credential cannot be verified.

examples.title: A credential with a structured issuer

rdfs:label: items
rdfs:comment: The members of an ActivityStreams Collection (or a CollectionPage), in no specified order.
notes: Use on a `Collection`/`CollectionPage`; for `OrderedCollection`/`OrderedCollectionPage`, prefer `as:orderedItems`. Either form may inline objects or list `@id` references; servers commonly paginate via `first`/`next` rather than returning all items in one document.

examples.title: A small Collection with inline items

rdfs:label: jabberID
rdfs:comment: A Jabber/XMPP identifier for the Agent.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF — a Jabber ID uniquely identifies its owner. The value is a bare JID string like `alice@jabber.example.org`, not a `xmpp:` URI. For other instant-messaging handles, see `vcard:hasInstantMessage`.

rdfs:label: keyword
rdfs:comment: A keyword or tag describing a DCAT Dataset or Catalog — repeated for multiple keywords.
notes: DCAT prefers repeated singular `dcat:keyword` literals (one per language tag) over schema.org's comma-separated `urn:solid:keywords` string. For controlled-vocabulary topical metadata, prefer `dcat:theme` with SKOS Concepts.

rdfs:label: keywords
rdfs:comment: Keywords or tags describing the resource — typically as a comma-separated string or a list.
notes: Schema.org accepts comma-separated text, an array of strings, or `schema:DefinedTerm` references. For ActivityStreams-style hashtag/mention attachments, use `urn:solid:tag`. For broader topical metadata, `urn:solid:subject` (dcterms).

rdfs:label: knows
rdfs:comment: A person known by the subject — a directed acquaintance relationship.
notes: Asymmetric by default: A knows B does not imply B knows A. Use repeatedly to enumerate the social graph. The FOAF tradition treats this loosely — any acknowledged acquaintance counts.

rdfs:label: knowsAbout
rdfs:comment: A topic the agent has expertise in or knowledge of.
notes: Use to declare expertise ("Alice knows about category theory") rather than mere interest (`urn:solid:topic_interest`) or a page about an interest (`urn:solid:interest`). Value can be a string keyword or a SKOS Concept / topic resource. Repeat for multiple areas of expertise.

rdfs:label: knowsLanguage
rdfs:comment: A language the person speaks, writes, or otherwise communicates in.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:language` (which is the language of a *resource*) — `knowsLanguage` is the languages an *agent* communicates in. Value is typically a BCP 47 tag (`"en"`, `"de-CH"`) or a `schema:Language` resource. Repeat for multiple languages.

rdfs:label: label
rdfs:comment: A human-readable name for a resource — short, plain text, suitable for UI display.
notes: The most-general human-name predicate in RDF. For people prefer `foaf:name` (mapped to `urn:solid:name`); for SKOS Concepts prefer `skos:prefLabel`; for documents prefer `dcterms:title`. Use `rdfs:label` for everything else (vocabulary terms, classes, properties, opaque resources).

rdfs:label: landingPage
rdfs:comment: A web page that gives access to a DCAT Dataset, its Distributions, and additional information.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:accessURL` (a Distribution-level access link): `landingPage` is the human-facing introduction page for the whole Dataset, where browsers go for context. Distinct from FOAF `urn:solid:homepage` which is for Agent homepages.

rdfs:label: language
rdfs:comment: A language of the resource — typically a BCP 47 tag.
notes: Use BCP 47 language tags as values (`"en"`, `"en-US"`, `"de-CH"`). For multilingual resources, repeat. JSON-LD documents can also express language directly on string literals via `@language` — this property is for declaring the resource's overall language(s).

rdfs:label: last
rdfs:comment: The final page of a paginated ActivityStreams Collection — the entry point for clients that want to start at the end (oldest activities, most recent post for chronologically reversed orderings).
notes: Optional companion to `as:first`. Useful when the Collection has stable bounds (an outbox with finite history, an archived event log) so clients can deep-link to the end without walking the whole chain. Servers may omit it for unbounded or live-growing Collections.

examples.title: Paginated outbox with first and last

rdfs:label: lastName
rdfs:comment: The last name of a person.
notes: Older sibling of `foaf:familyName` — kept for compatibility with legacy FOAF data. New profiles should prefer `urn:solid:familyName`. The first/last vs given/family terminology is culture-bound; treat them as equivalent in practice.

rdfs:label: latitude
rdfs:comment: The latitude of a location, in decimal degrees (WGS-84).
notes: Decimal degrees, positive north of the equator. Pair with `urn:solid:longitude` on a `urn:solid:GeoCoordinates` resource. For a single shorthand `geo:` URI carrying both, use `urn:solid:hasGeo`.

rdfs:label: license
rdfs:comment: A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource.
notes: Value should be the license document's IRI (e.g. an SPDX URL or a Creative Commons license page), not free text. For unstructured rights statements use `urn:solid:rights` instead. SPDX (`https://spdx.org/licenses/MIT`) and Creative Commons URLs are the most interoperable choices.

rdfs:label: liked
rdfs:comment: The Collection of Objects an ActivityPub Actor has liked — the Actor's history of `Like` activities, presented as a queryable list.
notes: Third side of the public-facing triad on an AP Actor (`followers`, `following`, `liked`). Often kept private — many servers expose a count via `totalItems` but withhold the items themselves. The reverse direction ("who liked this Object?") lives on the Object as `as:likes`.

examples.title: An Actor with a liked Collection

rdfs:label: locality
rdfs:comment: The locality (city, town, village) of an Address.
notes: City/town field of a vCard Address. Pair with `urn:solid:region`, `urn:solid:postal-code`, `urn:solid:country-name`. The schema.org equivalent is `schema:addressLocality` on a `urn:solid:PostalAddress`.

rdfs:label: location
rdfs:comment: The location associated with the subject — typically a Place, address, or geographic coordinates.
notes: Generic location predicate used on Events, Actions, Organizations. The value is typically a `urn:solid:Place`, `urn:solid:PostalAddress`, or `urn:solid:GeoCoordinates`. For a person's home region (intentionally fuzzy), use `urn:solid:basedNear` (FOAF). For structured postal addresses, `urn:solid:hasAddress` (vCard).

rdfs:label: loginEndpoint
rdfs:comment: The login endpoint URL for a Solid OIDC provider.
notes: Advertised by a Solid OIDC provider, points at the URL where users can initiate authentication. Most modern Solid OIDC implementations expose this via OIDC discovery (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`) rather than via this predicate, but the term remains useful for explicit declaration.

examples.title: OIDC issuer with a login endpoint

rdfs:label: logoutEndpoint
rdfs:comment: The logout endpoint URL for a Solid OIDC provider.
notes: Counterpart to `urn:solid:loginEndpoint`. Advertised by a Solid OIDC provider as the URL where users can sign out. Most modern Solid OIDC implementations expose this via OIDC discovery (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`'s `end_session_endpoint`) rather than via this predicate.

examples.title: OIDC issuer with login and logout endpoints

rdfs:label: longitude
rdfs:comment: The longitude of a location, in decimal degrees (WGS-84).
notes: Decimal degrees, positive east of the prime meridian. Pair with `urn:solid:latitude` on a `urn:solid:GeoCoordinates` resource. For elevation as well, schema.org provides `schema:elevation`.

rdfs:label: made
rdfs:comment: A thing the agent made — the inverse of `maker`.
notes: Use on an agent to point at things they made. The inverse `urn:solid:maker` goes the other direction (work → agent). Repeat to list multiple works. For richer attribution semantics, prefer `dcterms:creator` or `prov:wasAttributedTo`.

examples.title: Person and the document they made

rdfs:label: maker
rdfs:comment: An agent that made the subject — the inverse of `made`.
notes: Use on a document or work to point at the agent that made it. The inverse `foaf:made` goes the other direction (agent → work). For richer creator semantics with role and contribution type, prefer `dcterms:creator` or `prov:wasAttributedTo`.

rdfs:label: mappingRelation
rdfs:comment: Superproperty of all SKOS cross-scheme mapping relations — `exactMatch`, `closeMatch`, `broadMatch`, `narrowMatch`, `relatedMatch`. Asserts that two Concepts in different schemes are related, without specifying how.
notes: Use the most specific subproperty available — bare `mappingRelation` only when the kind of mapping is genuinely unknown. Distinct from `skos:semanticRelation` (which covers in-scheme relations like `broader`/`narrower`); mappingRelations cross scheme boundaries.

examples.title: A generic mapping between two concepts

rdfs:label: mbox
rdfs:comment: A personal mailbox — typically a mailto: IRI.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF: an mbox value uniquely identifies its owner, so two agents with the same mbox are the same agent. Prefer a `mailto:` IRI as the value, not a bare string. For a plain string email, see `vcard:hasEmail` or `schema:email`.

rdfs:label: mbox_sha1sum
rdfs:comment: The SHA-1 hash of the agent's mailbox URI — a privacy-preserving inverse-functional identifier.
notes: Inverse-functional like `foaf:mbox` but doesn't reveal the actual email address. Compute the SHA-1 of the lowercased `mailto:` URI (e.g. SHA-1 of `"mailto:alice@example.org"`). Two agents with the same `mbox_sha1sum` are the same agent. Modern profiles often skip both this and `mbox` for privacy.

rdfs:label: mediaType
rdfs:comment: The MIME media type of the object — `image/png`, `text/html`, etc.
notes: ActivityStreams' content-type label — typically attached to `as:content` (to declare the format of HTML vs plain text) or to attachments. Distinct from dcterms `urn:solid:format` only by namespace; carry the same string values (IANA media types).

examples.title: Note with explicit content media type

rdfs:label: mediator
rdfs:comment: An intermediary that mediates access to or use of the resource — typically for educational or curated content.
notes: From the educational-resources tradition: a teacher who selects and uses a textbook is a `mediator`. Used to express that the resource was filtered or curated by an intermediary before reaching its `urn:solid:audience`. Niche outside library/edu contexts.

examples.title: Course material with a teacher mediator

rdfs:label: medium
rdfs:comment: The material or physical carrier of the resource.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:format`: `medium` is the physical/material carrier (paper, vinyl, parchment), `format` is the file format or media type. A book may have format `application/pdf` and medium "paperback". Library and archive metadata uses both fields when both apply.

rdfs:label: member
rdfs:comment: An agent that is a member of the group.
notes: Use to enumerate the agents that belong to a group. Repeated to list multiple members. The subject should typically be a `foaf:Group`; the value can be any Agent (Person, Organization, Group, software).

rdfs:label: memberList
rdfs:comment: An ordered list of members of a SKOS OrderedCollection — preserves sequence in a way that the unordered `skos:member` cannot.
notes: Functional and required on a `skos:OrderedCollection`: exactly one `rdf:List` of Concepts, encoding their canonical order (chapter sequence, taxonomic ranking, presentation order). Use plain `skos:member` for unordered groups.

rdfs:label: memberOf
rdfs:comment: An Organization (or Group) the Agent is a member of — the inverse of `member`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:member` (the FOAF group → member relation, also re-used by ORG). Use on the Agent to enumerate the Organizations they belong to. For role-aware membership with start/end times, attach a `urn:solid:Membership` resource instead.

rdfs:label: membershipResource
rdfs:comment: The resource that membership triples for a DirectContainer or IndirectContainer are added to.
notes: Used on `urn:solid:DirectContainer` and `urn:solid:IndirectContainer` to identify *where* membership triples land. Pair with `ldp:hasMemberRelation` (the predicate to use) and `ldp:isMemberOfRelation` (the inverse). Not used on plain `BasicContainer`s.

examples.title: DirectContainer pointing at a membership resource

rdfs:label: mode
rdfs:comment: An access mode granted by a Web Access Control Authorization — Read, Write, Append, or Control.
notes: Repeat to grant multiple modes in one Authorization. Standard values are `acl:Read`, `acl:Write`, `acl:Append`, `acl:Control`. `Write` implies `Append`; `Control` is the meta-mode that lets the holder edit the .acl file itself.

rdfs:label: modified
rdfs:comment: The date the resource was last modified.
notes: Updated on every substantive edit; pair with `urn:solid:created` (set once). ISO 8601 (`xsd:dateTime` or `xsd:date`). For RDF Patch / streaming-update systems, the value typically reflects the most recent committed change.

examples.title: Document with creation and modification dates

rdfs:label: movedTo
rdfs:comment: On an ActivityStreams Actor, the new identity URI the Actor has migrated to — the forwarding address left behind on the old account.
notes: Forms the second half of the fediverse account-migration handshake. The *old* Actor sets `as:movedTo` pointing at the new identity; the *new* Actor lists the old in `as:alsoKnownAs`. Servers that see both sides confirmed automatically migrate followers; clients render the old account as redirected.

examples.title: An Actor that has migrated to a new server

rdfs:label: name
rdfs:comment: A name for the subject.
notes: The canonical display name. For structured names (given/family), use `foaf:givenName` and `foaf:familyName` directly until urn-solid ships equivalents.

rdfs:label: nameMap
rdfs:comment: Language-tagged variants of an ActivityStreams Object's `name` — keys are BCP 47 language tags, values are the localised name strings.
notes: Provide alongside (or instead of) `as:name` when the Object has translations. Standard fediverse pattern for multilingual content. Clients SHOULD pick the best match for the user's locale; servers MAY mirror one entry into `as:name` as a fallback for non-aware consumers.

rdfs:label: narrowMatch
rdfs:comment: A SKOS mapping asserting that a Concept in another scheme is narrower than this Concept.
notes: Cross-scheme version of `urn:solid:narrower`. Inverse of `urn:solid:broadMatch`. Use across SKOS schemes when you want to say "the closest narrower concept in *that* vocabulary is this one".

rdfs:label: narrower
rdfs:comment: A narrower (child) SKOS Concept in a hierarchy — the inverse of `broader`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:broader`. Use to enumerate child concepts in a hierarchy. SKOS treats the relation as transitive only inside one ConceptScheme — for transitive descendants use `skos:narrowerTransitive`. Repeat for multiple children.

rdfs:label: next
rdfs:comment: The next page in an ActivityStreams CollectionPage chain — the URL the client follows to advance through pagination.
notes: Present on every CollectionPage except the last. Clients walk pagination by repeatedly fetching `next` until it's absent — that's the termination signal, not a count check against `totalItems`. Pair with `prev` for bidirectional scrolling.

examples.title: A CollectionPage linking to the next page

rdfs:label: nick
rdfs:comment: A short informal nickname for the subject — typically a chat handle or screen name.
notes: For informal handles (IRC, IM, screen names) rather than legal or display names. A subject may have many nicknames across different contexts. Use `urn:solid:name` for the canonical display name.

rdfs:label: notation
rdfs:comment: A symbolic identifier for a SKOS Concept within a particular notation system (Dewey numbers, ISBN-style codes, taxonomy IDs).
