notes: Unlike `skos:prefLabel` (a human-readable string in a natural language), `skos:notation` is a typed literal whose datatype identifies the notation system — e.g. a Dewey Decimal code typed as `<http://example.org/dewey>` is distinct from a UDC code with the same digits. A Concept may carry multiple notations from different schemes.

rdfs:label: oidcIssuer
rdfs:comment: The OpenID Connect issuer that this WebID trusts to authenticate it.
notes: The Solid OIDC trust anchor: the value is the issuer URL of the OpenID Provider whose tokens this WebID will accept. A WebID may list multiple `oidcIssuer` values for redundancy. Distinct from the older FOAF `urn:solid:openid` (a document-based pre-OIDC scheme).

examples.title: WebID with a Solid OIDC issuer

rdfs:label: onProperty
rdfs:comment: On an OWL Restriction, the property being constrained.
notes: Required on every `owl:Restriction`. Pair with the actual constraint predicate — `owl:someValuesFrom`, `owl:allValuesFrom`, `owl:hasValue`, `owl:cardinality`, `owl:minCardinality`, `owl:maxCardinality` — to express "on property X, the constraint is Y".

examples.title: A restriction on the knows property

rdfs:label: oneOf
rdfs:comment: On an ActivityStreams Question, the exclusive set of answer choices — voters pick exactly one.
notes: Use exactly one of `oneOf` (single-choice poll) or `anyOf` (multiple-select poll) on a Question — never both. Each option is typically a `Note` whose `name` carries the displayed text; `replies.totalItems` is then the vote count for that option.

rdfs:label: openid
rdfs:comment: An OpenID identifier for the Agent — a document used to verify the Agent's identity.
notes: Inverse-functional in FOAF — an OpenID document uniquely identifies its Agent. Predates Solid OIDC; for modern Solid pods use `solid:oidcIssuer` instead, which points at the OpenID Connect issuer URL.

rdfs:label: orderedItems
rdfs:comment: The ordered members of an ActivityStreams OrderedCollection or OrderedCollectionPage — sequence is significant.
notes: Use on `OrderedCollection`/`OrderedCollectionPage`; for unordered collections use `as:items`. The JSON array order is the canonical order — for a chronologically sorted outbox, that's typically newest-first. Servers paginate ordered collections via `first`/`next` just like unordered ones.

rdfs:label: organization-name
rdfs:comment: The name of the organization the person is affiliated with — typically the employer.
notes: vCard's quick organization-name string — useful when you only have the company name as text. For a structured affiliation, prefer `urn:solid:worksFor` pointing at a `urn:solid:Organization` resource.

rdfs:label: origin
rdfs:comment: Where an ActivityStreams Activity comes *from* — the source side of a movement, transfer, or invitation, complementing `as:target` (the destination).
notes: Used most often with `Move`, `Travel`, `Add`, and `Remove` — together with `target` it forms the source-and-destination pair. `Move` an item from `origin` to `target`; `Travel` from `origin` to `target`. Distinct from `as:actor` (who did it) and `as:object` (what was acted on).

rdfs:label: outbox
rdfs:comment: The OrderedCollection of Activities an ActivityPub Actor has published — POSTing to it is how the Actor sends new Activities to the network.
notes: Two roles in ActivityPub: GET reads the Actor's published-Activity history (paginated); POST is the client-to-server submission endpoint — the Actor's own client posts here, and the server fans the Activity out to recipient inboxes. Mirror of `as:inbox` (which is the receive side).

examples.title: An Actor with an outbox endpoint

rdfs:label: owner
rdfs:comment: An agent that owns the resource — typically used to declare pod ownership.
notes: Solid-specific ownership predicate — declares the WebID(s) that own a pod or resource. Pod operators can read this to determine who has full control. Distinct from `dcterms:rightsHolder` (broader copyright/IP ownership) and `urn:solid:creator` (who made it).

rdfs:label: ownerOf
rdfs:comment: A pod or resource the agent owns — the inverse of `owner`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:owner` — declared on a WebID to enumerate the pods/resources the user owns. Useful for cross-pod ownership claims and discovery. Often co-asserted with `urn:solid:storage`.

rdfs:label: page
rdfs:comment: A document about the subject — any page that describes or discusses it.
notes: More general than `urn:solid:homepage` — any page about the subject, not just the canonical one. Repeat to list multiple. For the inverse "this page is about", see `foaf:topic` (page → subject).

examples.title: Person with a page about them

rdfs:label: parent
rdfs:comment: A parent of the person.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:children`. Repeat for multiple parents (biological, adoptive, step-). Sensitive personal data; consider access control. Distinct from `dcterms:isPartOf`/`hasPart` which encode whole-part composition rather than family relations.

rdfs:label: partOf
rdfs:comment: Identifies the parent Collection that an ActivityStreams CollectionPage is a slice of — lets the client jump from a page back to the whole.
notes: Required on every CollectionPage so consumers can recover context — "this page belongs to which Collection?" Without `partOf`, a client that lands on a page mid-pagination has no way to know what whole it's a slice of, which breaks deep-linking and resume-from-here flows.

examples.title: A CollectionPage referencing its parent Collection

rdfs:label: pastProject
rdfs:comment: A project the person is no longer active on.
notes: Use to retain history when a person's involvement ends. Repeat to list multiple. Move from `urn:solid:currentProject` here when the person stops being involved. The value can be any resource — typically a `urn:solid:Project` or a Document describing it.

rdfs:label: phone
rdfs:comment: A phone number for the agent — typically a `tel:` IRI.
notes: FOAF's lightweight phone predicate. The value is conventionally a `tel:` URI, mirroring `foaf:mbox`'s `mailto:` style. For typed numbers (work/home/cell) prefer `urn:solid:hasTelephone` (vCard); for plain string values prefer `urn:solid:telephone` (schema.org).

rdfs:label: postIn
rdfs:comment: Links a Post to the Organization in which it sits.
notes: Identifies which Organization owns the position. Use alongside `org:heldBy` (current holder) and an optional `org:role` (the abstract role the Post embodies) to fully describe a seat in an org chart.

examples.title: A Post and the Organization it sits in

rdfs:label: postal-code
rdfs:comment: The postal code (ZIP code) of an Address.
notes: vCard's postal-code field. Stored as a string because postal codes are not always numeric (UK "SW1A 1AA", Canada "K1A 0B1"). Schema.org equivalent is `schema:postalCode`.

rdfs:label: prefLabel
rdfs:comment: The preferred lexical label for a SKOS Concept — its canonical name in a given language.
notes: Exactly one `prefLabel` per language tag per Concept (SKOS integrity rule). Use language-tagged literals for multilingual vocabularies. Synonyms go under `urn:solid:altLabel`; non-display strings (typos, misspellings used for search) go under `urn:solid:hiddenLabel`.

rdfs:label: preferencesFile
rdfs:comment: A document containing the subject's private preferences.
notes: Conventionally a private document linked from the WebID profile, holding application preferences and other personal settings. Should be access-controlled (only the user can read/write). Apps discover it via the WebID and follow links from it (e.g. to the private TypeIndex).

rdfs:label: preferredUsername
rdfs:comment: An ActivityPub Actor's preferred short username — the local part used in `@user@host` mention syntax.
notes: The handle, not the display name: `as:preferredUsername` is `alice` (used in webfinger and `@alice@host` mentions); `as:name` is "Alice Smith" (the human-readable display string). Lowercase, alphanumeric, no spaces — meant for routing and addressing, not presentation.

examples.title: An Actor with a handle and display name

rdfs:label: prev
rdfs:comment: The previous page in an ActivityStreams CollectionPage chain — the URL the client follows to scroll back through pagination.
notes: Mirror of `as:next`. Optional but recommended — without `prev`, a client that lands on a deep page can only walk forward, never back. Servers commonly omit on the first page (where it would have no value).

examples.title: A middle page exposing both next and prev

rdfs:label: preview
rdfs:comment: An object that provides a preview of the subject — typically a thumbnail image or a snippet.
notes: ActivityStreams' general-purpose preview slot — useful for link unfurling, video posters, document covers. Distinct from `urn:solid:thumbnail` (specifically a smaller image of an Image) and `urn:solid:icon` (small avatar). The value can be any AS Object with a `urn:solid:url`.

rdfs:label: primaryTopic
rdfs:comment: The primary topic of a document — the thing the document is principally about.
notes: A document has at most one primary topic. WebID profile documents canonically have their subject Person as `foaf:primaryTopic`. The inverse is `foaf:isPrimaryTopicOf`. For documents about multiple things at equal weight, use `foaf:topic` (no primacy) instead.

rdfs:label: privateTypeIndex
rdfs:comment: The private TypeIndex for a WebID — an access-controlled registry of where personal data of each type lives.
notes: Linked from a WebID, points at the user's access-controlled TypeIndex. Used by trusted apps (after auth) to discover where personal data is stored. Pair with `urn:solid:publicTypeIndex` for the world-readable counterpart.

examples.title: WebID pointing at its private TypeIndex

rdfs:label: profileSubject
rdfs:comment: The subject (Person) that a profile document is about.
notes: Solid-specific name for the relation FOAF expresses as `foaf:primaryTopic`. Use on a profile document to point at the Person it describes. Most existing data uses `foaf:primaryTopic`; this is the modern Solid-namespaced equivalent.

rdfs:label: proof
rdfs:comment: A cryptographic proof attached to a VerifiableCredential or VerifiablePresentation — what verifiers check to confirm the document hasn't been tampered with and was signed by the claimed party.
notes: An Object carrying the proof type (e.g. `Ed25519Signature2020`, `DataIntegrityProof`), the signature value, and metadata: when, by which key (`verificationMethod`), and for what purpose (`proofPurpose`). Defined in the W3C Security Vocabulary; used unchanged by VC, DID Document signing, and ActivityPub HTTP Signatures.

examples.title: A credential with a proof block

rdfs:label: provenance
rdfs:comment: A statement of any changes in ownership and custody of the resource since its creation — its provenance trail.
notes: dcterms's narrative provenance pointer — for human-readable custody/transformation history. For machine-actionable provenance graphs, use the PROV vocabulary (`urn:solid:wasDerivedFrom`, `urn:solid:wasGeneratedBy`, `urn:solid:Bundle`). Both can coexist: dcterms:provenance gives the headline, PROV gives the audit trail.

rdfs:label: publicTypeIndex
rdfs:comment: The public TypeIndex for a WebID — a world-readable registry of where public data of each type lives.
notes: Linked from a WebID, points at the user's publicly-readable TypeIndex. Distinct from `urn:solid:privateTypeIndex` (access-controlled, only readable by the user and their authorized apps). Public type registrations are typically for data the user intends to share (public contact info, published content).

examples.title: WebID pointing at its public TypeIndex

rdfs:label: publications
rdfs:comment: A document listing the publications of the person.
notes: Points at a publications-list document (CV-style, ORCID page, etc.) — not at the publications themselves. For the works directly, use `urn:solid:made` (FOAF) or `dcterms:creator` on each work.

examples.title: Person pointing at their publication list

rdfs:label: published
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object was published — when it went public.
notes: ActivityStreams' publication timestamp — the wall-clock time a post went out. Distinct from `urn:solid:created` (when the resource was constructed) and `urn:solid:issued` (dcterms' formal publication date). ISO 8601 `xsd:dateTime`.

rdfs:label: publisher
rdfs:comment: An entity responsible for making the resource available.
notes: The publisher distributes or hosts the resource — distinct from the creator (who made it). For self-published content the same agent may fill both roles, but model them as separate triples to keep the semantics clear.

rdfs:label: qualifiedAssociation
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV Association linked to the activity — adds role and plan to a `wasAssociatedWith` relation.
notes: Use to attach a `urn:solid:Association` that names which Plan an Agent followed and what role they took during an Activity. Pattern: keep both the unqualified `wasAssociatedWith` triple AND the qualified form.

rdfs:label: qualifiedAttribution
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV Attribution linked to the entity — adds role and timing to a `wasAttributedTo` relation.
notes: Use to attach a `urn:solid:Attribution` resource that qualifies the basic `urn:solid:wasAttributedTo` link with role (author, editor, photographer, contributor). Pattern: keep both the unqualified `wasAttributedTo` triple AND the qualified form for SPARQL convenience.

rdfs:label: qualifiedDerivation
rdfs:comment: A qualified PROV Derivation linked to the entity — adds role, activity, and other context to a `wasDerivedFrom` relation.
notes: Use to attach a `urn:solid:Derivation` resource that qualifies the basic `urn:solid:wasDerivedFrom` link with role, plan, or activity. Pattern: when you need richer derivation metadata, keep both the unqualified `wasDerivedFrom` triple (for SPARQL convenience) AND the qualified form.

rdfs:label: qualifiedGeneration
rdfs:comment: Links an Entity to the `prov:Generation` instance describing the activity, time, and role in which the Entity was created.
notes: The qualified counterpart to `prov:wasGeneratedBy`. Use when a plain `wasGeneratedBy` triple isn't enough — to record the time of generation, the role the Entity played in the activity, or to attach further provenance to the generation event itself.

rdfs:label: qualifiedInvalidation
rdfs:comment: Links an Entity to a `prov:Invalidation` instance describing the activity, time, and circumstances in which the Entity ceased to exist.
notes: The qualified counterpart to `prov:wasInvalidatedBy`. Use when a plain triple is insufficient — to record the time of invalidation, the role the Entity played, or to attach further provenance to the invalidation event itself (deletion log, retention policy reference).

rdfs:label: qualifiedUsage
rdfs:comment: Links an Activity to a `prov:Usage` instance that adds detail (which entity, when, in what role) to a plain `prov:used` link.
notes: Use when the bare `prov:used` triple isn't enough — e.g. an Activity used the same Entity twice in different roles, or you need to record the time of use, or attach a `prov:Role` reified link. The Usage instance carries the extra context; the Activity points at it via `qualifiedUsage`.

rdfs:label: radius
rdfs:comment: The radius around an ActivityStreams Place's centre point that the Place covers — a circular area, in metres unless `as:units` says otherwise.
notes: Describes *area* (the size of the Place); `as:accuracy` describes *uncertainty* (how confident we are in the centre). A neighbourhood might have a 2000-metre radius with 90% accuracy; a GPS-pinned café might have a 50-metre radius with 95% accuracy.

rdfs:label: range
rdfs:comment: Declares the type of values an RDF property is meant to take — its object type.
notes: Object-side constraint. `foaf:knows` has range `foaf:Person`. May also point at an XSD datatype (`xsd:string`, `xsd:dateTime`) for literal-valued properties. Like `domain`, multiple range declarations mean intersection — the value must be an instance of all listed types.

rdfs:label: references
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource.
notes: Use to record outbound citations or references. The inverse is `dcterms:isReferencedBy`. For richer bibliographic citations with structured metadata, prefer `dcterms:bibliographicCitation` (string) or attach a separate `dcterms:BibliographicResource`.

rdfs:label: region
rdfs:comment: The region (state, province, prefecture) of an Address.
notes: vCard's sub-national administrative region — US states, UK counties, Indian states, Japanese prefectures. Often a 2-letter code ("CA", "NY") for US data. Schema.org equivalent is `schema:addressRegion`.

rdfs:label: rel
rdfs:comment: The link relation type of an ActivityStreams Link — semantic role of the connection (canonical, alternate, prev, next, …).
notes: Values are IANA-registered link relation types from <https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/> (`canonical`, `alternate`, `enclosure`, `self`, `next`, etc.) — same vocabulary HTML and HTTP `Link:` headers use. Repeat to express multiple relations on one Link.

rdfs:label: related
rdfs:comment: A SKOS Concept that is associatively (non-hierarchically) related to the subject Concept.
notes: Use for non-hierarchical conceptual associations — "category-theory related-to functional-programming". Symmetric in SKOS. Distinct from `urn:solid:relation` (dcterms generic relation between resources) and from `broader`/`narrower` (hierarchical).

rdfs:label: relatedMatch
rdfs:comment: Asserts an associative (non-hierarchical) link between two SKOS Concepts in different schemes — the cross-scheme analogue of `skos:related`.
notes: Use when two Concepts are *meaningfully associated* but neither narrower nor broader than the other — e.g. "Birds" in one taxonomy associated with "Aviation" in another. Distinct from `closeMatch` (similar meaning) and `exactMatch` (interchangeable); a `relatedMatch` is a see-also, not a substitute.

rdfs:label: relation
rdfs:comment: A related resource — generic relation when more specific predicates don't apply.
notes: The most generic dcterms relation predicate — fallback when more specific dcterms relations (`hasPart`, `references`, `source`, `replaces`, `isVersionOf`) don't fit. Avoid when possible; the specific terms carry more semantic weight. For a similarly-loose RDF predicate, see `rdfs:seeAlso`.

rdfs:label: replaces
rdfs:comment: A related resource that the described resource supplants, displaces, or supersedes.
notes: Use to record that this resource is the new official version of an older one (a v2 spec replacing v1, a new policy replacing the prior one). The inverse is `dcterms:isReplacedBy`. For term-level supersession inside the urn-solid registry itself, the schema's `supersededBy` field on a term file is the right place.

rdfs:label: replies
rdfs:comment: A Collection of objects that are responses to the subject — the reverse of `inReplyTo`.
notes: The inverse of `urn:solid:inReplyTo`. Lives on the parent object and points at a `urn:solid:Collection` (or `OrderedCollection`) of replies. ActivityPub servers compute this by aggregating inbound `inReplyTo` from across the network.

rdfs:label: requires
rdfs:comment: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function or coherence.
notes: Use for hard dependencies — software that needs another library, a document that requires its referenced datasets, an API spec requiring an auth scheme. Repeat for multiple dependencies. The inverse is `dcterms:isRequiredBy`.

rdfs:label: result
rdfs:comment: Describes the result produced by an ActivityStreams Activity — for example, the booking returned by a Reservation.
notes: `as:result` describes what the Activity *produced*; `as:object` describes what it *acted on*. A Like activity has the liked Note as its `object` and may have nothing meaningful as its `result`; a booking activity has the requested room as `object` and the confirmed booking as `result`.

rdfs:label: rights
rdfs:comment: Information about rights held in and over the resource — copyright, IP, access restrictions.
notes: Free-form rights statement (e.g. "Copyright 2026 Acme Corp. All rights reserved.") or a link to a `dcterms:RightsStatement` resource. For machine-actionable permissions, use `urn:solid:license` with an SPDX or Creative Commons URL.

jsonld.urn:solid:rights: Copyright 2026 Alice Liddell. All rights reserved.

rdfs:label: rightsHolder
rdfs:comment: An agent owning or managing rights over the resource — the copyright holder, IP owner, or licensing controller.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:creator` (who made it) and `urn:solid:owner` (Solid pod ownership): `rightsHolder` is specifically about IP/copyright control. A work-for-hire has a creator (the worker) and a separate rightsHolder (the employer).

rdfs:label: role
rdfs:comment: The job role or function the person performs within an organization.
notes: vCard's role string — typically a job title or function ("Senior Engineer", "Treasurer"). For schema.org-flavored data, prefer `schema:jobTitle`. For PROV-grade role-in-Activity attribution, use `prov:hadRole`.

rdfs:label: sameAs
rdfs:comment: An external reference URL that unambiguously identifies the subject — typically a profile or canonical page on another site.
notes: Distinct from OWL's `owl:sameAs`: schema.org's `sameAs` is a soft "this is also at" reference (Wikipedia page, social profile, registry entry), without the strong identity-equivalence semantics that OWL reasoners apply. Use schema's form for everyday cross-site identity hints; use OWL's form only when you mean true identity equivalence in a reasoning sense.

rdfs:label: schoolHomepage
rdfs:comment: A homepage of a school (or other educational institution) the person attended.
notes: FOAF's lightweight "I went to that school" pointer — the value is the school's homepage URL, not a structured Organization resource. For richer educational-history data, prefer `urn:solid:alumniOf` pointing at a `schema:EducationalOrganization`. Repeat for multiple schools.

rdfs:label: scopeNote
rdfs:comment: A SKOS note clarifying the intended scope or usage of a Concept — "use this for X but not Y".
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:definition` (the meaning itself) — `scopeNote` is editorial guidance for catalogers and users about when to apply the Concept. Mirrors the disambiguation-style notes on urn-solid term files themselves.

jsonld.urn:solid:scopeNote: Use for the mathematical theory; for the database concept of "category" use the `taxonomy/category` concept instead.

rdfs:label: seeAlso
rdfs:comment: Points at a related resource that may carry additional information about the subject — a generic "more about this here" link.
notes: Weakest of the cross-reference predicates: makes no claim about authority or canonicality, just relevance. Use when you want to surface a related resource without asserting it's a definition or an equivalence. `isDefinedBy` and `owl:sameAs` are stronger statements when those apply.

examples.title: A resource pointing at related material

rdfs:label: semanticRelation
rdfs:comment: The SKOS superproperty for any conceptual relation between Concepts — `broader`, `narrower`, `related`.
notes: Rarely asserted directly — superproperty of `skos:broader`, `skos:narrower`, `skos:related`, and their transitive variants. Useful when reasoning generically over any conceptual link, or when you have a relation you can't classify more specifically.

rdfs:label: servesDataset
rdfs:comment: A Dataset that a DCAT DataService makes available.
notes: Repeat once per Dataset the service exposes — a single SPARQL endpoint or API may publish many. The inverse direction (`dcat:Dataset` → service) is not standard; lookups go through the service.

rdfs:label: sha1
rdfs:comment: The SHA-1 cryptographic hash of the resource's content.
notes: Use to record content integrity for files, datasets, or releases. SHA-1 is cryptographically weakened — for new data, prefer SHA-256 (`schema:sha256` or a custom predicate). Value is the lowercase hex digest of the bytes.

rdfs:label: shares
rdfs:comment: A Collection of `Announce` activities (shares / boosts / reposts) directed at an Object — discoverable from the Object itself.
notes: The standard ActivityPub way to expose "who reshared this?" without mailing every share to every reader. Servers append each `Announce` of an Object to its `shares` Collection; clients dereference the Collection to count and display shares. Mirrors `as:likes` for like activities.

examples.title: A Note exposing its shares Collection

rdfs:label: sibling
rdfs:comment: A sibling of the person — sharing at least one parent.
notes: Symmetric — if A is sibling of B, B is sibling of A. Use repeatedly for multiple siblings. Sensitive personal data; consider access control before publishing.

rdfs:label: someValuesFrom
rdfs:comment: On an OWL Restriction, asserts that at least one value of the constrained property must be an instance of a given class — an existential quantifier.
notes: Reads as "there is at least one value on this property in this class." Use to define classes like "Articles that have at least one Author who is a Person." Pairs with `allValuesFrom` (universal — every value is in the class).

examples.title: A class requiring at least one Person author

rdfs:label: source
rdfs:comment: A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
notes: Use to record the upstream origin of derived works (translations, adaptations, summaries, scraped data). For PROV-grade derivation chains with role and timing, prefer `prov:wasDerivedFrom`. Repeat to list multiple sources.

rdfs:label: spatial
rdfs:comment: The spatial coverage of the resource — what places it is about or applies to.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:location` (where the resource itself *is*) — `spatial` is the geographic *subject* of the resource (a study about Wales, a dataset covering the Pacific). Value is typically a `dcterms:Location` or a `urn:solid:Place`. Pair with `urn:solid:temporal` for the time dimension.

rdfs:label: specializationOf
rdfs:comment: Asserts that one PROV Entity is a more constrained version of another — same identity, narrower aspect (e.g. a single revision of a document is a specialization of the document as a whole).
notes: Specialization preserves identity — the specialized Entity *is* the general one viewed at finer granularity (e.g. "the CSS file as of commit abc" specializes "the CSS file"). Contrast with `prov:wasDerivedFrom`, which links *different* entities causally, and `prov:alternateOf`, which links two specializations of a common general entity.

examples.title: A document version as a specialization

rdfs:label: spouse
rdfs:comment: The person to whom the subject is married.
notes: Symmetric in practice — if A is the spouse of B, B is the spouse of A. Sensitive personal data; consider access control before publishing. For other family relations, schema.org provides `parent`, `children`, `sibling`, `relatedTo`.

rdfs:label: startTime
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object begins.
notes: ISO 8601 datetime marking when an Event, Activity, or other time-bounded object begins. Pair with `urn:solid:endTime` (or `urn:solid:duration`). For PROV-grade activity timing, prefer `prov:startedAtTime`.

examples.title: Event with start and end times

rdfs:label: startedAtTime
rdfs:comment: The time at which the activity started.
notes: PROV-grade activity-start timestamp. Use on a `prov:Activity` to record when execution began. ActivityStreams `urn:solid:startTime` is the equivalent for AS Events; pick by domain — PROV for processes, AS for calendar events.

rdfs:label: status
rdfs:comment: A free-form status string for the agent — e.g. "online", "away", or a custom message.
notes: FOAF's lightweight presence/status field — IM-style "away", "busy", or a free-form message ("writing the registry"). For ActivityPub-style profile bios, `as:summary` on the actor is more common today.

rdfs:label: storage
rdfs:comment: The root of a personal data store (Solid pod) for the subject.
notes: From the PIM space vocabulary. The value is the root URL of the user's pod (a Container). A WebID may list multiple `pim:storage` values when the user has multiple pods. Apps use this to discover where to read/write data on behalf of the user.

examples.title: WebID with a pod storage root

rdfs:label: streams
rdfs:comment: Additional Collections an ActivityPub Actor exposes beyond the standard inbox/outbox/followers/following — extension points for application-specific feeds.
notes: An open-ended list of named or anonymous Collections — bookmarks, drafts, an alternate-channel outbox, anything the application needs. Clients SHOULD discover and label these from the Actor's published metadata; servers SHOULD treat them as fully addressable like the standard endpoints.

rdfs:label: street-address
rdfs:comment: The street address of an Address — number, street name, unit.
notes: vCard's street-address line. Note the hyphen in the source name is preserved. Pair with `urn:solid:locality`, `urn:solid:region`, `urn:solid:postal-code`, `urn:solid:country-name` on a `vcard:Address`. For a schema.org-flavored address, use `schema:streetAddress` on a `urn:solid:PostalAddress`.

rdfs:label: subClassOf
rdfs:comment: Asserts that one class is a subclass of another — instances of the subclass are also instances of the superclass.
notes: Transitive: if A is a subclass of B and B of C, then A is a subclass of C. Reasoners use this to infer that a `urn:solid:Person` is also a `urn:solid:Agent`. A class may be a subclass of multiple parents (multiple inheritance is permitted in RDFS).

examples.title: Person is a subclass of Agent

rdfs:label: subOrganizationOf
rdfs:comment: The parent Organization that this OrganizationalUnit is part of — the inverse of `hasSubOrganization`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasSubOrganization`. Use on a unit to point at its parent — useful for traversal up an org chart. Typically declared once (a unit has one parent), but ORG allows multiple parents for matrix structures.

examples.title: Engineering team pointing at parent company

rdfs:label: subPropertyOf
rdfs:comment: Asserts that one property is a refinement of another — every triple using the subproperty also (logically) holds with the superproperty.
notes: Transitive, like `subClassOf`. Reasoners use it to climb the property hierarchy — knowing `prov:wasRevisionOf` is a subproperty of `prov:wasDerivedFrom` lets a query for derivations also find revisions. Use to model specialised/general predicate pairs.

examples.title: wasRevisionOf is a subproperty of wasDerivedFrom

rdfs:label: subject
rdfs:comment: A topic of the resource — typically expressed as keywords, key phrases, or controlled-vocabulary terms.
notes: Use repeatedly to enumerate subjects. Values can be string keywords, but a SKOS Concept or controlled-vocabulary term is preferred for interoperability. For "the principal thing this document is about", `urn:solid:primaryTopic` is more specific.

rdfs:label: summary
rdfs:comment: A natural-language summary of the object — typically shorter than its `content`.
notes: ActivityStreams' short-form digest — in Mastodon and other fediverse clients this is the content-warning / spoiler-text field. Pair with `urn:solid:content` for the full body. For long-form bibliographic abstracts, prefer `urn:solid:abstract`; for generic resource descriptions, `urn:solid:description`.

rdfs:label: summaryMap
rdfs:comment: Language-tagged variants of an ActivityStreams Object's `summary` — keys are BCP 47 language tags, values are the localised summary strings.
notes: On the fediverse, `summary` is also used as the content warning / spoiler text — `summaryMap` lets that warning be translated alongside the post body. Pair with `contentMap` so the visible warning matches the language of the content the user will reveal.

examples.title: A Note with localised content warning

urn:solid:contentMap.en: I cannot believe what just happened…
urn:solid:contentMap.fr: Je n'arrive pas à croire ce qui vient de se passer…

rdfs:label: tableOfContents
rdfs:comment: A list of subunits of the resource — chapters, sections, parts.
notes: Free-form text or list — typically a serialized TOC. For a structured part-of relation pointing at separate resources for each subunit, prefer `urn:solid:hasPart` (then each part has its own resource and metadata).

examples.title: Book with a table of contents

jsonld.urn:solid:tableOfContents: Ch 1: Down the Rabbit-Hole; Ch 2: The Pool of Tears; Ch 3: A Caucus-Race; ...

rdfs:label: tag
rdfs:comment: An object that is part of the private secondary audience of the subject — typically a hashtag or @mention.
notes: ActivityStreams' inline-mention slot — used by ActivityPub posts to attach `as:Hashtag` or `as:Mention` references that surface in the body. Repeat to list multiple tags. Distinct from `urn:solid:subject` (broader topical metadata) and `urn:solid:audience` (intended recipients).

rdfs:label: target
rdfs:comment: The target of the activity — the indirect object of the action.
notes: Where `as:object` is the direct object of an Activity, `as:target` is the indirect object — the destination, recipient, or container. For `as:Add`, `as:Move`, `as:Remove`: the collection items are added to / moved into / removed from. For `as:Like`: rarely used (object is enough).

examples.title: Add a note to a collection

rdfs:label: telephone
rdfs:comment: A telephone number for the subject — typically as a plain string.
notes: Schema.org's simple string-valued phone predicate ("+44-20-1234-5678"). Distinct from `urn:solid:hasTelephone` (vCard, uses a `tel:` URI for stricter parsing). Use whichever matches your data flavor.

rdfs:label: temporal
rdfs:comment: The temporal coverage of the resource — what time period it is about or applies to.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:date`/`urn:solid:created` (when the resource was made) — `temporal` is the time period the resource is *about* (a 19th-century history dataset, a Q1-2026 financial report). Value is typically a `dcterms:PeriodOfTime` or an ISO 8601 interval string. Pair with `urn:solid:spatial`.

rdfs:label: temporalResolution
rdfs:comment: The minimum time between samples in a DCAT Dataset or Distribution — the granularity of the time axis.
notes: Encoded as an `xsd:duration` (`PT1H` = hourly samples, `P1D` = daily, `PT15M` = 15-minute). Crucial when the same dataset is published at multiple cadences — clients pick the right Distribution based on the resolution they need, not just the format.

examples.title: A dataset with hourly temporal resolution

rdfs:label: text
rdfs:comment: The textual content of the resource — used by Comments, Answers, Questions, and other text-bearing schema.org types.
notes: Schema.org's general-purpose text-body predicate. Distinct from `urn:solid:articleBody` (Article-specific) and `urn:solid:content` (ActivityStreams). Use on `urn:solid:Comment`, `urn:solid:Answer`, `urn:solid:Question`, or any schema.org type that bears prose.

rdfs:label: theme
rdfs:comment: A main category of a DCAT Dataset — typically a SKOS Concept from a controlled-vocabulary theme list.
notes: Distinct from `urn:solid:keyword` (free-text tags): `dcat:theme` points at structured `urn:solid:Concept`s from a published theme vocabulary. The EU Data Theme vocabulary (`http://publications.europa.eu/resource/authority/data-theme/`) is the canonical example. The ConceptScheme is declared via `dcat:themeTaxonomy` on the parent Catalog.

rdfs:label: thumbnail
rdfs:comment: A thumbnail rendering of the image — a smaller version for previews.
notes: Use on a full-size image to point at a smaller preview rendition. Both subject and object should be `urn:solid:Image`. For richer image-object metadata (width, height, content URL), schema:ImageObject + schema:thumbnail carry more fields.

rdfs:label: to
rdfs:comment: The primary recipients of the object — the wire-level "send to" addresses.
notes: ActivityPub's primary delivery list — receivers in `to` are visible recipients and the activity is delivered to their inboxes. Use the symbolic IRI `https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams#Public` to make a post world-readable. For semantic targeting ("intended for friends"), use `urn:solid:audience` instead.

rdfs:label: topConceptOf
rdfs:comment: The SKOS ConceptScheme of which the Concept is a top-level entry-point — the inverse of `hasTopConcept`.
notes: Inverse of `urn:solid:hasTopConcept`. Use on the Concept side when you want top-concept membership declared without editing the ConceptScheme. Implies `inScheme` membership for the same scheme.

rdfs:label: topic
rdfs:comment: A thing the document is about — the inverse of `page`.
notes: A document can have many `topic`s with no implied primacy. Use `urn:solid:primaryTopic` when one topic is the principal subject (one per document). The inverse `urn:solid:page` goes from subject → document.

rdfs:label: topic_interest
rdfs:comment: A thing the agent is interested in — points at the resource itself, not at a page about it.
notes: Use when the interest target is itself a resource (a Person, Organization, Project, concept). For "a page about something I'm interested in", use `urn:solid:interest`. Note the underscore in the source name is preserved.

rdfs:label: totalItems
rdfs:comment: The total number of members in an ActivityStreams Collection — the size the client would see if all pages were concatenated.
notes: Authoritative count even when the Collection is paginated and only a subset of `items` is materialised in any given response. Drives "42 likes" / "123 followers" UI without forcing the client to walk the entire pagination chain.

rdfs:label: trustedApp
rdfs:comment: On a Solid pod owner's profile, an application origin granted broad trust — typically permitted to read or write across the pod without per-resource ACL grants.
notes: A pre-WAC-AC pattern, still widely used: each `trustedApp` value carries `acl:origin` (the app's URL origin) and `acl:mode` (the modes granted). Solid CSS, NSS, and others honour this for app-level authorisation. Newer specs (ACP) supersede it but legacy pods still depend on it.

examples.title: Profile granting an app Read+Write trust

rdfs:label: type
rdfs:comment: Asserts that a resource is an instance of a class — the predicate behind JSON-LD's `@type` keyword.
notes: The most-used predicate in all of RDF. JSON-LD authors usually write `@type: "Person"`; the underlying triple is `<subject> rdf:type urn:solid:Person`. A subject can have many types simultaneously (multi-typing is normal in RDF, unlike most class-based languages).

rdfs:label: unitOf
rdfs:comment: The parent Organization that this OrganizationalUnit belongs to — inverse of `hasUnit`.
notes: Sub-property of `urn:solid:subOrganizationOf` constrained to point at the parent of an OrganizationalUnit. Inverse of `urn:solid:hasUnit`. Functionally equivalent to `subOrganizationOf` for OrganizationalUnit subjects.

rdfs:label: units
rdfs:comment: The unit of measurement for the linear dimensions of an ActivityStreams Place — `radius` and `altitude` are interpreted in this unit.
notes: Standard values: `cm`, `feet`, `inches`, `km`, `m`, `miles`, or any custom URI. Default is metres when `units` is absent. Applies to `radius` and `altitude`; latitude/longitude are always degrees.

rdfs:label: updated
rdfs:comment: The date and time the object was last updated.
notes: ActivityStreams' last-edit timestamp. Functionally equivalent to `dcterms:modified` (`urn:solid:modified`), but stays in the AS namespace for ActivityPub-flavored data. ISO 8601 `xsd:dateTime`. Pair with `urn:solid:published` (first-published time).

examples.title: Note with publication and update timestamps

rdfs:label: url
rdfs:comment: An ActivityStreams Object's primary URL — the human-facing page where the Object can be viewed in a browser, distinct from its `@id` (the AP-facing identifier).
notes: On Mastodon-style fediverse content, `@id` is `https://mastodon.example/users/alice/statuses/123` (server-to-server) while `as:url` is `https://mastodon.example/@alice/123` (the user-facing permalink). Clients render `url` to readers and use `@id` for federation. May be a string or an `as:Link` — the Link form lets you supply rel/type/hreflang.

examples.title: A Note with a separate user-facing URL

rdfs:label: used
rdfs:comment: An entity used by the activity — an input or dependency that existed before the activity started.
notes: PROV's input pointer: the activity consumed or referenced the entity. Pair with `prov:wasGeneratedBy` on the output side to form a full input-activity-output chain. For typed usage with roles or timing, qualify with `prov:qualifiedUsage`.

rdfs:label: valid
rdfs:comment: The date or period of validity of the resource — when it should be considered current and applicable.
notes: Use for time-bounded resources — coupons, certificates, regulations, embargoed reports. Value is typically an ISO 8601 interval. Distinct from `urn:solid:available` (when it became obtainable) and `urn:solid:issued` (when it was published).

rdfs:label: verificationMethod
rdfs:comment: The cryptographic key (or other verification material) the verifier should use to check a proof — typically a fragment of a DID Document.
notes: Value is an IRI that dereferences to a verification method object — usually `<did>#<keyId>` in a DID Document. The verifier resolves the key, then uses it to validate the signature in the surrounding `proof`. Same property is reused by VC proofs and DID Document key registrations.

examples.title: A proof referring to a verification method

rdfs:label: version
rdfs:comment: The version designation of the resource — typically a string like "2.0" or "v3.1.4".
notes: Schema.org's version-string predicate. Distinct from `urn:solid:hasVersion` (which points at *another resource* that's a version) and `urn:solid:isVersionOf` (the inverse). Use `version` for the bare string identifier of *this* resource's version.

rdfs:label: wasAssociatedWith
rdfs:comment: An agent that had a role or responsibility in the activity — performed it, oversaw it, or was implicated in it.
notes: PROV agent-to-Activity relation — distinct from `wasAttributedTo` (which links an Entity to its responsible Agent). Use `wasAssociatedWith` for who ran the build, who reviewed the change, who triggered the pipeline. Qualify via `prov:qualifiedAssociation` to add a role and a Plan.

examples.title: Build associated with a software agent

rdfs:label: wasAttributedTo
rdfs:comment: An agent to which the entity is attributed — without claiming the agent performed any specific action.
notes: PROV's lightweight "this is associated with that agent" relation — weaker than `prov:wasGeneratedBy` (which requires a specific Activity). For richer attribution with a role, qualify via `prov:qualifiedAttribution` and a `prov:Attribution` resource.

rdfs:label: wasDerivedFrom
rdfs:comment: An entity from which the subject entity was derived — a precursor or input.
notes: Use to record the upstream entity a derived work descends from — translations, summaries, transformed datasets. Repeat to list multiple sources. For typed derivation (revision, quotation, primary-source), pair with `prov:qualifiedDerivation` and a `prov:Derivation` resource.

rdfs:label: wasEndedBy
rdfs:comment: An Entity that ended a PROV Activity — the signal, completion event, or termination input that caused the Activity to stop.
notes: The mirror of `prov:wasStartedBy`. Use when termination has an identifiable trigger (a stop signal, a deadline document, a downstream consumer indicating completion). For plain wall-clock time, use `prov:endedAtTime`.

examples.title: Build activity ended by a cancel signal

rdfs:label: wasGeneratedBy
rdfs:comment: The PROV activity that generated the entity — the production event responsible for its existence.
notes: PROV-grade pointer from an entity (the result) at the activity (the process). Pair with `prov:generatedAtTime` for the timestamp. For lighter-weight "this was created" semantics without a separate Activity resource, `urn:solid:created` (a date) is sufficient.

examples.title: Document generated by a build run

rdfs:label: wasInfluencedBy
rdfs:comment: The most general PROV influence relation — asserts that one Entity, Activity, or Agent had some effect on another, without specifying the kind of influence.
notes: The supertype of every PROV influence link (`wasDerivedFrom`, `wasGeneratedBy`, `used`, `wasAssociatedWith`, `actedOnBehalfOf`, etc.). Use only when the kind of influence is unknown or deliberately unspecified — otherwise the more specific subproperty carries more meaning to consumers.

rdfs:label: wasInformedBy
rdfs:comment: An activity exchanged information with the prior activity — without naming the entity that flowed between them.
notes: PROV's lightweight "this activity follows that one" relation — used when you want to record temporal/causal ordering between activities without modelling the intermediate Entity. For full traceability, prefer chaining `urn:solid:used` and `urn:solid:wasGeneratedBy` through explicit Entities.

examples.title: Build informed by previous test run

rdfs:label: wasInvalidatedBy
rdfs:comment: The PROV Activity that invalidated (deleted, retracted, expired) the Entity.
notes: PROV's invalidation pointer — the inverse-in-time of `prov:wasGeneratedBy`. Records that an Entity ceased to exist at a particular Activity. Pair with `prov:invalidatedAtTime` for the timestamp. ActivityStreams' lighter equivalent for social data is `as:Tombstone`.

rdfs:label: wasQuotedFrom
rdfs:comment: An Entity is a quotation, excerpt, or reproduction of part of another Entity — the source remains identifiable and authoritative.
notes: A subproperty of `prov:wasDerivedFrom`. Use when content is *literally* lifted from the source (a pull-quote in an article, an excerpted paragraph, a re-shared image) rather than transformed. The source is generally expected to be cite-able and verifiable.

rdfs:label: wasRevisionOf
rdfs:comment: An Entity that this Entity is a revision of — same nominal identity, updated content (a v2 of a document, a re-issued dataset).
notes: A subproperty of `prov:wasDerivedFrom` — every revision is a derivation, but a revision specifically replaces the prior version while keeping the same name/role. Use for explicit version chains (v1 → v2 → v3); use plain `wasDerivedFrom` when the new entity is a transformation rather than an update.

rdfs:label: wasStartedBy
rdfs:comment: An Entity that started a PROV Activity — the trigger or input whose existence caused the Activity to begin.
notes: Identifies the *triggering* Entity (a request, a sensor reading, a message). Not the agent who acted (`wasAssociatedWith`) and not an upstream activity that handed off (`wasInformedBy`). For wall-clock time, use `prov:startedAtTime`.

examples.title: Build activity started by a webhook payload

rdfs:label: weblog
rdfs:comment: A weblog (blog) of the subject — the document the agent publishes posts to.
notes: Points at the blog as a whole, not at an individual post. An agent may have multiple weblogs (personal, work, project-specific). Use `urn:solid:homepage` for the main page about the agent rather than their writing feed.

rdfs:label: width
rdfs:comment: The width in pixels of an ActivityStreams Object — typically an Image, Video, or Link to a visual resource.
notes: In pixels, not CSS units. Always declare alongside `as:height` — both together let renderers compute aspect ratios and pre-reserve layout space, avoiding cumulative layout shift when media loads asynchronously.

rdfs:label: workplaceHomepage
rdfs:comment: A homepage of an organization the person works for.
notes: FOAF's lightweight "I work at that place" pointer — the value is the employer's homepage URL, not a structured Organization resource. For richer employment metadata, prefer `urn:solid:worksFor` pointing at a `urn:solid:Organization`. Repeat for multiple workplaces.

rdfs:label: worksFor
rdfs:comment: An organization the person currently works for.
notes: Use for current employment relationships. For past employers, use `schema:alumniOf`. For looser group affiliations (clubs, mailing lists, project contributors), `urn:solid:member` is more apt — `worksFor` implies an employment-like commitment.
